connected-surfaces

Every graph or ownership connection stays within a tab; moving a chromium, filetree, opened editor, or owner moves its entire live connected component with matching wire previews.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Every connected surface stays in one tab

Prepare real connected surfaces

  1. Start an isolated workspace with SOURCE and TARGET tabs. Keep an unrelated terminal in each tab so both tabs survive every move.
  2. In SOURCE create an OWNER terminal, its connected filetree, a Neovim editor opened by that filetree, an HTML/image/PDF chromium preview opened by the filetree, and a second chromium created directly by OWNER. Connect another agent pane to the editor with a paused graph link. Do not connect the two unrelated terminals.
  3. Use real Neovim and chromium processes. The deterministic fixture may use an isolated Neovim configuration with its built-in explorer instead of downloading Fyler; this case tests live ownership and transfers, not plugin installation.
  4. Note every %N, terminal/editor PID, chromium PID, URL, and ownership link. Arrange different pane positions and sizes; zoom out to see the full group.

Move from the chromium

  1. Press the directly attached chromium's pane header, hover TARGET until it opens, and move into its canvas. Inspect the preview before releasing.
  2. The preview must carry OWNER, both chromiums, the filetree, its opened Neovim, and the linked agent, including every association wire and paused graph link. Neither unrelated terminal may appear in the carried group.
  3. Release. All six surfaces must be in TARGET. For every graph, chromium-owner, owner-filetree, and filetree-editor edge, assert that both endpoints have the same tab. Compare all pane offsets and sizes to the pointer-down snapshot.

Move from the filetree

  1. Drag the filetree header back into SOURCE using tab hover and content drop.
  2. Verify the same complete group moves, including the parent OWNER. Assert all connection endpoints are tab-local, all wire previews are present, and geometry, IDs, processes, editor contents and chromium pages survive.

Move from the opened Neovim and preview chromium

  1. Drag the opened Neovim header into TARGET. Its parent filetree, OWNER, chromiums and connected agent must follow; verify every link and process.
  2. Drag the filetree's preview-chromium header back into SOURCE. Perform the same checks. Being the child endpoint must never allow a connection across tabs.

Move from the owner and cancel

  1. Drag OWNER into TARGET. Verify the same group, geometry and live identities.
  2. Drag the linked agent toward SOURCE, inspect the complete preview, then press Escape. All membership, positions, connections and processes must be unchanged.
  3. Attempt API/CLI graph connections between the group and either unrelated terminal in another tab; they must fail without creating an edge.
  4. Open another file through the filetree after the moves: reuse the same live editor, in the same tab. Open another HTML preview and confirm its chromium stays with its controller. Independently opened, unconnected panes remain independent; unrelated OS subprocesses are not pane connections.
  5. Report PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED with before/preview/after/cancellation evidence for each starting surface. A parent-only move or mocked topology is insufficient.

# Every connected surface stays in one tab

## Prepare real connected surfaces

1. Start an isolated workspace with SOURCE and TARGET tabs. Keep an unrelated
   terminal in each tab so both tabs survive every move.
2. In SOURCE create an OWNER terminal, its connected filetree, a Neovim editor
   opened by that filetree, an HTML/image/PDF chromium preview opened by the
   filetree, and a second chromium created directly by OWNER. Connect another
   agent pane to the editor with a paused graph link. Do not connect the two
   unrelated terminals.
3. Use real Neovim and chromium processes. The deterministic fixture may use an
   isolated Neovim configuration with its built-in explorer instead of downloading
   Fyler; this case tests live ownership and transfers, not plugin installation.
4. Note every `%N`, terminal/editor PID, chromium PID, URL, and ownership link.
   Arrange different pane positions and sizes; zoom out to see the full group.

## Move from the chromium

1. Press the directly attached chromium's pane header, hover TARGET until it
   opens, and move into its canvas. Inspect the preview before releasing.
2. The preview must carry OWNER, both chromiums, the filetree, its opened Neovim,
   and the linked agent, including every association wire and paused graph link.
   Neither unrelated terminal may appear in the carried group.
3. Release. All six surfaces must be in TARGET. For every graph, chromium-owner,
   owner-filetree, and filetree-editor edge, assert that both endpoints have the
   same tab. Compare all pane offsets and sizes to the pointer-down snapshot.

## Move from the filetree

1. Drag the filetree header back into SOURCE using tab hover and content drop.
2. Verify the same complete group moves, including the parent OWNER. Assert all
   connection endpoints are tab-local, all wire previews are present, and geometry,
   IDs, processes, editor contents and chromium pages survive.

## Move from the opened Neovim and preview chromium

1. Drag the opened Neovim header into TARGET. Its parent filetree, OWNER,
   chromiums and connected agent must follow; verify every link and process.
2. Drag the filetree's preview-chromium header back into SOURCE. Perform the same
   checks. Being the child endpoint must never allow a connection across tabs.

## Move from the owner and cancel

1. Drag OWNER into TARGET. Verify the same group, geometry and live identities.
2. Drag the linked agent toward SOURCE, inspect the complete preview, then press
   Escape. All membership, positions, connections and processes must be unchanged.
3. Attempt API/CLI graph connections between the group and either unrelated
   terminal in another tab; they must fail without creating an edge.
4. Open another file through the filetree after the moves: reuse the same live
   editor, in the same tab. Open another HTML preview and confirm its chromium
   stays with its controller. Independently opened, unconnected panes remain
   independent; unrelated OS subprocesses are not pane connections.
5. Report PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED with before/preview/after/cancellation evidence
   for each starting surface. A parent-only move or mocked topology is insufficient.

disconnect-reroutes

Disconnecting terminal nodes removes orphaned reroute dots, preserves shared reroutes still in use, and supports undo/redo without resurrecting stale routes.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Disconnect removes orphaned reroute dots

Use a disposable Flat workspace with three terminals titled Source, Review, and Check. Advertise fixture Send/Receive ports; no LLM response is needed. Enter Overview so every wire and reroute is visible. Do not change personal sessions.

Single connection

Check that pane IDs and graph node IDs are the same canonical %N strings. Connect Source to Review using those IDs. Require the returned connection's from and to to use %N, and socket/edge keys to use %N/port and %N/send>%N/receive. Keep those identities unchanged through disconnect, undo/redo, and reconnect. Insert two reroute dots and move them away from the direct wire so their disappearance is obvious. Capture the connected state. Drag the connected input socket into empty space and release. Require the wire and both dots to disappear; clicking or hovering at the old dot positions must not reveal a selectable orphan. Undo once: restore the wire and exactly the same two dots at their original positions. Redo once: remove the wire and both dots again. Reconnect the same endpoints: the new wire must be direct, with no stale reroute path. Remove it before continuing.

Shared branches

Connect Source to Review and Check through one shared reroute, with an additional private reroute on the Review branch. Disconnect Review by dragging its input socket into empty space. Require the Review-only dot to disappear, while the shared dot and Check wire remain. Disconnect Check: the shared dot must now disappear too. Undo and redo the final disconnect; verify the shared route is restored and then removed without duplicates.

External disconnect

Create another routed Source-to-Review connection. Disconnect it through gft graph disconnect (the replay uses the same graph.disconnect request). Refresh/re-enter Overview. Require no route records, orphaned dots, stale selection, or revived path when reconnecting. Existing terminal shells must remain alive.

Evidence and result

Retain before/after images or a recording for visual review, including the remaining shared branch and both undo/redo outcomes. Inspect authoritative edges and visual route/reroute records as well as rendered dots. PASS requires both topology and visual checks; a headless replay establishes the topology assertions only.

Replay:

uv run tests/godot/test_dashboard.py test disconnect-reroutes

The replay sets up deterministic wiring/reroute fixtures in the real application, then drives input-socket disconnects and undo/redo through the actual UI. It does not call a model and does not claim live-agent coverage. Run its Markdown steps or record the replay for LLM visual review.

Graph editing

Wire geometry and animation

A projected 200px pane at quarter zoom must expose five separate outputs with non-overlapping 44px touch targets; mouse targets keep at least 28px spacing. An 80px pane must compact. Verify wire endpoints, unchanged graph data, and route-cache reuse as the expanded ports spread during zoom.

Graph authority

Run agent_graph_smoke.gd against the real app. Check read permissions, file references, completion deduplication and disconnect/reconnect. These transport contract fixtures are deterministic and do not claim to be real model runs.

system-notification

Native notification clicks select and fit the emitting pane, including across tabs and minimized windows.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Native notification activation

Run gft node system-notification in a pane and connect an output to Notify. Check the Ratatui defaults, edit/apply with Ctrl+Enter, and save with Ctrl+S using --config. Send an event and check the timestamped title/body log and native OS notification. Switch tabs or minimize Graffitty, then click: the original graph sender must be selected and fitted in its current window. Test a relay chain, close the origin to check fallback to the previous sender, and choose this_pane to focus the notification node. Repeated clicks stay fitted. Repeat with printf '\033]9;Task finished\007' in an ordinary terminal. Dismiss a notification and verify focus stays unchanged. Close the emitting pane before clicking and verify no replacement pane or crash. Exit the node after emission and verify its notification can still focus its existing pane.

Replay: replays/system-notification.gd, in Flat and Flat 2D. The replay exercises real terminal bytes, OSC parsing, the node, asynchronous helper responses, and pane navigation, OSC 99 capability/alive queries, numbered button replies, and close reports; only the native desktop banner is substituted. Also verify real banners and clicks on macOS, Windows, and Linux with notifications enabled.

# Native notification activation

Run `gft node system-notification` in a pane and connect an output to Notify.
Check the Ratatui defaults, edit/apply with Ctrl+Enter, and save with Ctrl+S using
--config. Send an event and check the timestamped title/body log and native OS notification. Switch tabs or minimize
Graffitty, then click: the original graph sender must be selected and fitted in its
current window. Test a relay chain, close the origin to check fallback to the
previous sender, and choose `this_pane` to focus the notification node.

Connected graphs stay inside a tab

Prepare a connected group

# Connected graphs stay inside a tab

## Prepare a connected group

1. Launch an isolated workspace with two tabs. In the first, create four panes
   named ALPHA, BRAVO, CHARLIE, and UNRELATED; name the second tab TARGET.
2. Register test nodes with an `out` output and an `in` input. Connect
   ALPHA → BRAVO and CHARLIE → BRAVO; pause the second connection. Leave
   UNRELATED and TARGET disconnected. Record every pane's `%N` and shell PID.
3. Arrange the source panes with visibly different positions and sizes. Zoom out
   until all three connected panes and their wires are visible. Record their
   rectangles before pressing any header. Enable tiling and physics in TARGET.

## Reject cross-tab connections

1. Send `graph.connect` requests from ALPHA to TARGET and TARGET to ALPHA,
   including a paused connection request. Use the real authenticated API/CLI.
2. Every request must fail with an explanation that connections stay within one
   tab. Compare the graph before and after: no edge or permission may be added.

## Preview and move the connected group

1. Press BRAVO's header, move within its source canvas, then hover TARGET's tab
   until it opens. Continue into TARGET's canvas without releasing.
2. The preview must show ALPHA, BRAVO, CHARLIE and both connecting wires,
   including the paused wire. UNRELATED must not appear in the carried preview.
3. Compare the preview to the rectangles recorded before pressing the header:
   all three panes must have the same translation, with unchanged sizes.
   TARGET's tiling must not split or rearrange the group.
4. Capture the preview, release, and wait for physics to settle. BRAVO, the
   dragged anchor, must land where previewed. Other floating group members
   retain their sizes and yield independently to reduce overlap with the
   destination tile, subject to keeping their drag handles reachable. Both connections remain intact. UNRELATED
   stays in the original tab, and TARGET stays in its destination tab.
5. Check every original PID and `%N`. No shell may restart. A new connection
   from the moved group back to UNRELATED must now be rejected.

## Move to a new tab and cancel a move

1. Record the group's current rectangles. Drag BRAVO's header onto empty space
   at the end of the tab bar. The placeholder must identify a connected group.
2. Release. One new tab must contain all three connected panes, at their
   pre-drag positions and sizes. TARGET and UNRELATED must stay behind.
3. Start another header drag, hover the original source tab, and enter its
   canvas. Capture the group preview, then press Escape before releasing.
4. Membership, connections, positions, and PIDs must remain unchanged.
5. Report PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with before/preview/after/cancellation evidence.
   Inspect the actual rendered panes and wires; protocol checks alone do not
   certify the visual preview. Other frontends require their own execution.

Android agent list and attention sound

android-chromium-crash-recovery

Stop the Chromium host, then a page renderer, on the server computer and verify the client alerts the user, restarts the browser in the same pane and reloads the crashed page.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Chromium crash recovery

Run uv run tests/android/test_android_runtime.py android-chromium-crash-recovery --serial SERIAL for the physical Android client, or use --simulated for the Mac Godot client. Build the current Android extension first with uv run --no-project tools/build_android.py.

The shared workspace scenario opens a Chromium pane and waits for its pixels. The runner then kills that Chromium's host process on the server computer (a desktop client stops it directly), as a fatal browser abort would end it. The client must post exactly one error notification and replace the frozen page with a message offering Restart. The scenario taps Restart; the same pane must relaunch with a new host process, stream new frames, hide the message and, when the client advertises hardware codecs, keep hardware video.

The runner then kills the relaunched host's page renderers, which leaves the browser running. The client must post exactly one error notification and show a crashed-page message offering Reload, not Restart. The scenario taps Reload; the page must get a new renderer, stream new frames and hide the message.

Finally the page is put in an endless script loop. The client must show "This page is not responding" with Reload; tapping it must load the page again and resume the stream. Processes are only ever SIGKILLed and the stuck page is not crashed, so the run leaves no crash report for macOS to show as a dialog. The original terminal must survive.

Fit the affected pane before each recovery tap and choose an exposed part of the button when floating controls overlap it. Floating controls retain their normal placement and hit priority.

Repeat in a narrow phone pane: the failure heading wraps within the pane and recovery/close actions flow into additional rows instead of extending beyond its clipped right edge.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Hardware browser backends on Android

Run uv run tests/android/test_android_runtime.py android-chromium-hardware-backend --serial SERIAL against a server with a working hardware video encoder, separately for Alloy and Chrome. The test requires an actual hardware decoder, checks continuous animation, changes rendition size without changing website layout, checks the final static update, then exercises native tabs, popups, title/URL updates and page colors. PNG cannot satisfy this test. Keep the recording, runtime state, logcat and CHROMIUM_HARDWARE_MOTION metrics. The animation warms up for two seconds, then must sustain at least 30 presented frames per second for ten seconds while the page itself runs at least 55 animation callbacks per second. Measure without screen recording for the performance gate, and capture a separate functional run when recording affects the device. Use the production authenticated network route for acceptance; ADB forwarding is useful for diagnosis but adds another transport hop.

The existing harness accepts GRAFFITTY_ANDROID_SERVER_HOST as the owner's reachable interface address to use that direct authenticated route while ADB controls the disposable APK. Set GRAFFITTY_TEST_SERVER to the current release binary and preserve route.json with the measurements.

For Windows NVIDIA validation, enable RUST_LOG=graffitty_video on the server. Its NVENC D3D11 diagnostics must show GPU input, encoded/scaled frames and no CPU readbacks for the video-only client. A simultaneous PNG observer deliberately requests readback and must be disconnected before this measurement.

android-chromium-multi-stream

Verify several moving browsers on one connection stay stable and responsive on a physical Android client.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Concurrent browser streams

Open three server browsers from the Android client as floating panes stacked down the view, each tall enough that its page stays readable (a phone's title and browser toolbar take about 114 of a pane's height; tiled slivers pause by design), and animate each page at display cadence. Every browser must be streaming, not paused, before measuring for fifteen seconds.

Each page draws full-frame noise, so the streams need real bandwidth. Every stream must keep its hardware decoder (no restart) and none may freeze: each presents at least 60% of the client's main-loop frame rate, capped at 20 fps. No main-loop interval may exceed 250 ms. Record the P95 interval; the absolute frame-time gate belongs to the single-stream hardware case. When the link cannot carry every stream at full quality, the server lowers each viewer's bitrate tier (chromium flow bitrate share= in the trace) instead of freezing a stream; a frame lost beyond datagram repair is acknowledged by the client and the next frame restarts the stream at a keyframe. Record each stream's presented and received frame rate, delivered kbps and decoded size, plus render statistics.

Set GRAFFITTY_TEST_SERVER to the current release binary and GRAFFITTY_ANDROID_SERVER_HOST to the owner's reachable interface for the direct authenticated transport. Run RUST_LOG=graffitty_video to retain the server's flow traces. Closing the browsers must preserve the server terminal.

android-chromium-navigation

Create a real server chromium, receive frames, click and type Unicode into its DOM, navigate Back/Forward, and close only the chromium.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Android chromium navigation

Create a real server chromium and receive frames. Aim the centered cursor at its unobstructed address field, double tap, edit with Cmd/Ctrl+A, and press Enter to navigate. Focus must survive the Android keyboard shrinking the workspace. Also verify Unicode DOM input, Back/Forward, and closing only the chromium. Open a second tab and drag the first tab past it with a touch: within three seconds the pane's tab strip must show the order the server confirms, rather than the previous order until the strip's timeout.

Adapted from headless remote chromium. The shared implementation is chromium_navigation in tests/client_scenarios/workspace.gd; setup may use normal application commands while touch-specific interactions use Godot screen-touch events. A fresh standalone server owns every terminal, chromium and graph in this case.

Fit the browser in the available workspace before checking hardware video negotiation. Tiny overview panes intentionally pause video and show a PNG preview; that preview alone cannot establish decoder failure or a hardware-streaming pass.

Run the actual APK:

mise exec -- uv run tests/android/test_android_runtime.py android-chromium-navigation --serial emulator-5580

Run the identical scenario in the thin Mac Godot wrapper:

mise exec -- uv run tests/android/test_android_runtime.py android-chromium-navigation --simulated

Every assertion must pass, all touch contacts must be released, and the original server PTY must survive. Unexpected engine errors or diagnostic dialogs fail the case. Retain runtime-state.json, client/logcat logs and the complete APK screen recording. The Mac wrapper validates shared UI behavior, not Android IME, Keystore, lifecycle or GPU behavior.

android-chromium-scroll-stability

Repeatedly scroll real Chromium to both edges with wheel and touchpad input while checking decoded frames and browser responsiveness.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Chromium scroll stability

Run uv run tests/android/test_android_runtime.py android-chromium-scroll-stability --serial SERIAL for the physical Android client, or use --simulated for the Mac Godot client. Build the current Android extension first with uv run --no-project tools/build_android.py.

The shared workspace scenario loads a tall colored page and sends production ChromiumSession wheel and pan-gesture input. Three round trips per input mode verify every top/bottom DOM position, continued hardware video delivery, connection health, and three nonblack pixels across the presented top edge after settling. A fixed color marker changes at each endpoint; the decoded texture must reach that color within the assertion deadline, so a stale colored frame cannot pass. Clients advertising hardware codecs must retain a negotiated video codec throughout; PNG fallback fails the test. The original terminal must survive browser close.

Retain runtime state, logs, and recording. Each CHROMIUM_SCROLL_SAMPLE records presented frame count, codec, GPU sharing state, elapsed time, and observed interframe gap. These gaps exclude trailing idle and assertion waits and are diagnostic, not a throughput guarantee. Input events exercise the production browser adapter but are synthesized inside Godot; this case does not validate Android's physical gesture recognizer. Endpoint pixel checks do not rule out transient black strips during motion.

android-chromium-touch

Drag a real Chromium page with one finger like mobile Chrome, then tap it to click.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Chromium touch

Run uv run tests/android/test_android_runtime.py android-chromium-touch --serial SERIAL for the physical Android client, or use --simulated for the Mac Godot client. Build the current Android extension first with uv run --no-project tools/build_android.py.

The shared workspace scenario fits a real Chromium pane and loads a tall page with a click counter. Touch contacts go through the production MobilePointer recognizer:

  • One finger drags the page upward and holds still before lifting, so no fling adds distance. The page must scroll as far as the finger moved, measured in page pixels from the pane's displayed size, within 25%.
  • The drag must neither click nor select text. Chromium pages always scroll with one finger; the terminal's scroll-finger preference does not apply to them.
  • A quick tap at the pane's center must click the page exactly once, near the center of its viewport.

Retain runtime state and logs. CHROMIUM_TOUCH_DRAG records the scroll position, the expected distance and the displayed rectangle; CHROMIUM_TOUCH_TAP records the click coordinates.

The shared workspace scenario fits a real Chromium pane and loads a tall page with a click counter. Touch contacts go through the production `MobilePointer` recognizer:

- One finger drags the page upward and holds still before lifting, so no fling adds distance. The page must scroll as far as the finger moved, measured in page pixels from the pane's displayed size, within 25%.
- The drag must neither click nor select text. Chromium pages always scroll with one finger; the terminal's scroll-finger preference does not apply to them.
- A quick tap at the pane's center must click the page exactly once, near the center of its viewport.

Retain runtime state and logs. `CHROMIUM_TOUCH_DRAG` records the scroll position, the expected distance and the displayed rectangle; `CHROMIUM_TOUCH_TAP` records the click coordinates.

android-client-controls

Android menu and keyboard parity, with bottom terminal status preserved during zoom

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Touch controls and terminal title masking

Connect to a Mac server, then a Windows or Linux server. The accessory keyboard always offers Esc, Ctrl, Alt, Tab, Shift and arrows; it never requires Command or Option. Open Shell, Edit, View and Sessions. Verify New Tab, New Chromium, new panes, Close Pane, Copy, Paste, Find, Overview, Fit to Pane and Messages are available. Use an external keyboard: Ctrl+Shift+C/V copy/paste while plain Ctrl+C still interrupts the terminal. Activate a new pane through the menu.

Run a terminal application with a status line at the bottom. Zoom out until the title grows over the top rows and the icons disappear, then zoom back in. The terminal content must not shift or shrink. Its last row stays visible, the grid size stays unchanged, and only the top rows are covered by the title. Inspect actual rendered pixels, not just visibility flags. Repeat with the keyboard open.

The automated shared scenario checks menu coverage, modifier hints, unchanged terminal geometry/grid, and rendered coloured text on the bottom row across zooms.

android-device-stress

Check phone-specific GPU memory, touch delivery, and suspend/resume behavior that a VM cannot establish.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Device Stress

Runtime: Android. Physical device required.

Report PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with evidence. This procedure needs recorded LLM/manual execution. The automated APK cases cover shared client logic, English Gboard input and basic lifecycle, but do not establish this additional coverage as passing.

Requires a physical phone; keep this within the Android-runtime suite but mark emulator-only execution BLOCKED for this case.

  1. Record model, Android version, GPU/renderer, screen density, and APK identity. Connect to an isolated server containing several panes, graphs, and terminal images.
  2. Repeatedly pinch, pan, fit panes, switch tabs, and show/hide the keyboard. Measure application/graphics memory and capture crash/exit reasons. Verify the mobile render-target cap is retained.
  3. Background/foreground and lock/unlock repeatedly. On foldables, fold/unfold with a connection and keyboard active.
  4. Verify actual multitouch cancellation, OEM keyboard behavior, small-text appearance, and controls near gesture-navigation edges.
  5. Look for GPU fence failures, low-memory kills, stale surfaces, or stuck input. Preserve logs and screenshots with the result.

An emulator can detect some rendering/lifecycle failures, but cannot certify the phone's GPU driver, memory pressure, touch hardware, thermal behavior, or OEM integration.

android-direct-touch

Touch titles and drag node wires directly; verify client-local chrome, cursor shape, and stable typing with IME.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Direct Android touch

Single taps activate the control under the finger. Drag pane titles and node output sockets directly to their destinations. Double-tap a title to fit its pane. Two-finger pinch keeps the existing moving-center behavior and cancels any one-finger drag. There is no center cursor.

Terminal content scrolls with one finger by default; double-tap-and-drag selects. Use View → Terminal Touch Scrolling to switch between One Finger and Three Fingers. The latter permits ordinary one-finger selection. In both modes, adding a second finger cancels any pending selection and starts pinch navigation without copying.

At a pane's client-local fit scale, its header actions must be visible and readable. They hide below half that fit scale, independently of the desktop/server view. Typing and opening the IME must keep the terminal cursor visible without rewriting saved navigation each animation frame. Insert/command cursor shapes must survive streamed output and reconnect snapshots.

Run uv run tests/android/test_android_runtime.py android-direct-touch --serial SERIAL. Retain the APK video, state checks, and logcat. The simulated wrapper covers direct touch routing but not the native IME.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Dock-aware camera and cursor

Use the existing disposable Android-runtime client/server fixture. Open Agents and Sessions through registered actions (retain Agents if already open by default), open Resource Monitor, and commit them through the production dock layout. The separate android-list-docking case covers drag routing.

A real PTY program positions a steady cursor at opposite terminal corners. With a left sidebar, right sidebar, two sidebars, resized sidebars, top/bottom Resource Monitor docks alone and together with sidebars, and then no docks, test 1.15×/2× typing zoom (select typing zoom mode explicitly; adaptive framing has its own content-dependent target). Verify both vertical reservations and pointer-region exclusion. Also grow/shrink each horizontal dock while zoomed and check cursor containment on every sampled frame. Check the entire projected cursor cell against the unobstructed content rectangle and inspect actual framebuffer pixels, not only camera state. Close the default Status Line to isolate each dock reservation. After committing a horizontal drop, set its row to 120 pixels: the drop itself installs the floating panel height.

The raw PTY cursor fixture redraws on SIGWINCH as well as key input, keeping the requested corner when a dock reflows the grid.

Typing Unicode through a Godot key event or ADB text injection is not evidence that IME composition works. Exercise the actual installed IME. Check additional OEM keyboards on a phone.

On Flat 2D startup, restore the remembered pane before activating a terminal; selecting the first pane in tree order would overwrite the saved focus before the workspace opens. Cover a remembered pane with stable ID %1 appearing second in tree order.

LLM suite specification

Android list docking and presentation isolation

Use the existing disposable Android-runtime client/server fixture. Open Agents and Sessions through registered commands. Resize dock width and stack height with the invisible touch dividers, starting at the center and both edges of the full configured gap. No horizontal bar, floating resize border or corner triangle is painted. Agents/Sessions use dense spacing with no empty footer; Add server is absent on mobile. Repeat while floating: the title stays in place and unfolding restores the window size. A canceled tap and a drag that returns to its starting point must not toggle folding. android-main-area-keyboard

The active Android client sizes Main View to its usable screen, reflows rows above the keyboard, and stays in Main View through keyboard and orientation changes.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Android main area and keyboard

Use the production Android Servers entry point with an isolated server. Keep Fit main view to this client enabled. A direct connection that bypasses the server manager does not cover this regression.

  1. Connect in portrait, then landscape, and verify the viewport has the requested orientation. The most recently active client must claim the shared main area. Its width and height must match the Android content surface after subtracting visible tab/tool bars, docked panels and keyboard space. Measure their actual edges independently of the production fit helpers. The floating menu does not reserve a full-width row. Check the server's acknowledged area, not just a local camera fit. Do not retain a desktop-shaped main area with letterboxing.
  2. Let a second client claim a different aspect ratio. The Android client must follow that area while idle, then reclaim its own usable dimensions on an actual touch. The other client must observe that change without repeatedly taking ownership back. Keep the same terminal process throughout.
  3. Enter Main View and put readable output at the terminal bottom. Open the native keyboard using the keyboard button. The main area must become shorter and its aspect ratio must change to match the remaining space above the IME and accessory key bar. Terminal rows reflow; this is not uniform camera shrinkage of the previous desktop rectangle. Width and font size remain unchanged. The bottom content moves upward and remains visible.
  4. Main View must stay selected throughout keyboard opening, typing and closing. Sample the transition as well as the final frame: no saved overview/pan state may be introduced by keyboard insets. Close the keyboard and verify the full usable main area and row count return. Repeat twice in both orientations.
  5. Start from a deliberately panned/zoomed view, open and close the keyboard, and verify it does not reset to Main View. Panes and content keep their place on screen: the keyboard covers the lower part and only the main area changes size. Nothing pans to reveal the cursor, and closing the keyboard restores the same view. In landscape, include a keyboard that hides the menu and tab bar. No terminal or tab is recreated.

Retain the native recording, geometry checkpoints, screenshots and process logs. Review bottom-row readability and movement in the recording; a final screenshot cannot prove transition continuity. Any unexpected diagnostic is a failure. Desktop simulation covers the layout/claim logic with supplied inset heights. Enable canvas scaling and preserve the phone's aspect ratio inside the fixed recording canvas so both orientations exercise different logical dimensions. Output assertions must tolerate terminal row wrapping, and command echo alone must not satisfy them. Only an APK run certifies the native keyboard and Android surface dimensions.

LLM suite specification

Android messages copy

Long-press the intentional Unicode diagnostic, use Android’s native Select all and Copy actions, and verify the full text reaches the clipboard. Open log must open an in-app native selectable log viewer. Close it, dismiss the panel, and verify no stale shortcut interception. Focusing a connection footer button during keyboard layout changes must not produce a scroll-ancestor error.

Adapted from messages-copy. The shared implementation is messages_copy in tests/client_scenarios/workspace.gd; setup may use normal application commands while native text selection and its contextual toolbar are exercised through UIAutomator on Android. A fresh standalone server owns every terminal, chromium and graph in this case.

The native log viewer must use translated title and Close labels without accessing Godot nodes from Android's UI thread. Opening and closing it must leave the diagnostic/error log empty apart from the intentional fixture. The harness reads Select all and Copy from Android's localized resources and targets the dialog's positive button by resource ID, so the device language stays unchanged.

Run the actual APK:

mise exec -- uv run tests/android/test_android_runtime.py android-messages-copy --serial emulator-5580

Run the identical scenario in the thin Mac Godot wrapper:

mise exec -- uv run tests/android/test_android_runtime.py android-messages-copy --simulated

Every assertion must pass, all touch contacts must be released, and the original server PTY must survive. Unexpected engine errors or diagnostic dialogs fail the case. Retain runtime-state.json, client/logcat logs and the complete APK screen recording. The Mac wrapper validates shared UI behavior, not Android IME, Keystore, lifecycle or GPU behavior.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Native Android Ctrl shortcuts

Run on an ARM64 emulator or phone with Gboard English selected. This case taps the actual installed keyboard and Graffitty's accessory Ctrl button, and sends Android key chords through ADB. It does not inject Godot input events.

  1. Connect the disposable APK to an isolated server and focus its terminal.
  2. Tap accessory Ctrl and Gboard's equals, plus, minus, and zero keys. Verify font changes and one-shot modifier release, including after typing a word and switching to the symbol keyboard.
  3. Verify Android Ctrl+=, Ctrl+Shift+=, Ctrl++, Ctrl+-, and Ctrl+0.
  4. Read three raw PTY bytes from accessory Ctrl+U, plain u, and Android Ctrl+U. Require exactly 15 75 15; a visual pressed state alone is insufficient.
  5. Tap Esc and Tab, arm Ctrl/Alt/Shift together for one input, then tap each modifier twice to lock it. Type repeatedly, tap each again to release, and type plain text. Require the exact PTY bytes and retain screenshots of the normal, one-shot, locked, and released key row.
  6. Retain native event traces, screenshots, video, and assertions. Fail on any unexpected diagnostic and preserve the fixture server's original PTY.

Use android-text-size for floating-button targeting and Chrome zoom coverage. This native case complements those shared scenarios, which synthesize Godot events and cannot independently verify the Android input bridge.

   normal, one-shot, locked, and released key row.
6. Retain native event traces, screenshots, video, and assertions. Fail on any
   unexpected diagnostic and preserve the fixture server's original PTY.

LLM suite specification

Android pane resize

Apply three different pane sizes through the client resize command; verify authoritative server grids and unchanged neighbor grids. Then place the neighbor below the floating pane, clear of its touch grips (floating panes keep part of their header reachable, so a narrow phone pulls a far-right neighbor back over the pane), and drag all four edges and four corners with a finger starting 26 screen pixels outside the floating pane, at both reduced and increased zoom. Verify the requested dimensions change, the opposite edge stays anchored, the camera and neighboring grid stay unchanged, and release ends the resize. A second finger must cancel and restore the original rectangle.

Move a floating pane slightly outside Main, navigate to its right edge (a phone cannot show the whole pane), then resize that edge until its center crosses back inside Main. Repeat with tiling disabled and with a tiled neighbor. Only the grabbed edge may change: the pane must keep its floating/stashed membership, opposite edge, and camera framing throughout the drag, release, and server acknowledgment. Neighbors and saved tile proportions must stay unchanged. Only a deliberate move back into Main may rejoin the layout; resizing and cancellation are not drops.

Touch targets are invisible: no handle icons are added. The edge target extends mostly into empty canvas, stays screen-sized through zoom, and must not intercept another pane's content. Mouse targets retain their existing behavior. After returning both panes to Main and enabling tiling, drag a shared divider starting 20 screen pixels off its center; it must resize the tiles without detaching them. On a phone the two tiles can be narrower than their minimum width; the divider must still move, keeping each tile at least a quarter of the shared width.

android-retained-transitions

Both built-in worlds are selectable on mobile; Ctrl+D closes a real remote shell while Push/Pull retains native drawing state through source destruction and releases it after landing.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Retained tab transitions

Run uv run tests/android/test_android_runtime.py android-retained-transitions --serial SERIAL against a current Android build. Use --simulated instead of --serial SERIAL to execute the same scenario in the desktop GPU renderer.

The production remote manager connects to a disposable standalone owner. In Flat 2D and Flat 3D, open a second tab, print colored text, and deliver Ctrl+D through the terminal input route with Push/Pull.

While presentation time is held, the owner must close the shell and the client must free its original viewport. Each outgoing terminal layer must retain a native drawing view that redraws the colored text after increasing its requested resolution. Resume motion and require every retained target to be freed after landing. The original shell must still accept input.

All assertions, diagnostic checks and engine-error checks must pass. Preserve the runtime state, logs and APK screen recording. Inspect the continuous motion; these state/pixel checks alone do not certify frame pacing or physical keyboard delivery. Android starts in Flat 2D, exposes both built-in worlds in the World menu, and enables an isolated 3D world when Flat 3D is selected. Returning to Flat 2D must release the 3D rendering viewports and preserve the original terminal. Native desktop window handoffs and 3D toolbar departures are covered by desktop tests.

android-sidebar-pinch

Pinch the workspace with one finger on a docked sidebar and one on the main area, without breaking sidebar taps, sidebar scrolling or a pane drag.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Android pinch across a docked sidebar

Use the existing disposable Android-runtime client/server fixture. Open Agents through its registered command so that it docks into the left sidebar, and move the camera off the fitted frame, whose detent would pull a small pinch back. Inject touch through the window, so that the platform's emulated mouse and the dock's own input handlers take part.

  1. Rest finger 0 on the sidebar content, then put finger 1 on the main area. Both now belong to one workspace gesture. The sidebar received exactly a press, a canceled emulated-mouse release and a canceled touch. Spread finger 1 along the line through both fingers: the workspace zooms in and the point under the sidebar finger stays under it. Move and lift both: the sidebar receives nothing more.
  2. Rest finger 0 on the main area past the pointer grace, then put finger 1 on the sidebar content. The sidebar never sees finger 1; the pinch zooms.
  3. Start a pane title drag, then touch the sidebar. The drag stays held and keeps following its finger, while the second finger scrolls the sidebar.
  4. Scroll the sidebar with finger 0, then touch the main area: the sidebar finger is not taken and keeps scrolling. Rest finger 0 on the sidebar for longer than the yield window, then touch the main area: not taken either. The view does not change in either case.
  5. With a finger resting on the main area, touch the dock's resize edge and then its title: neither joins, and the canceled touches change no width, placement or fold state.

The original PTY survives and no contact or button remains held.

This covers injected touchscreen events on the recorded device or desktop simulation, not physical two-hand feel. Check GE-08 in tests/e2e/gestures.md for the remaining sidebars, bands, widths and landing delays.

android-system-ui

Verify the Android system boundaries used by the client.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

System Ui

Runtime: Android. Emulator or physical device.

Report PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with evidence. This procedure needs recorded LLM/manual execution. The automated APK cases cover shared client logic, English Gboard input and basic lifecycle, but do not establish this additional coverage as passing.

  1. Use an isolated connection, with terminal output and a deliberately displayed Graffitty messages panel.
  2. Copy terminal/message text through the client's available copy action, then paste into another Android app. Copy English, Korean, emoji, and multiline text from that app and paste into the focused terminal. Check exact server text.
  3. Exercise Android Back with a client dialog and with the system keyboard open; verify only the intended layer closes.
  4. Exercise any supported external-link or log-opening action through the Android intent resolver. A desktop shell-open call is not evidence for this boundary.
  5. Exercise Android split-screen and lock/unlock, including with the keyboard visible. Verify controls avoid actual status/navigation bars, display cutouts, and keyboard insets in portrait and landscape.
  6. On a test environment configured for the supported network path, interrupt and restore Android connectivity while connected. Verify the reconnect path and server session continuity. If testing Tailscale, exercise the actual Android VPN app; a local loopback server only validates the transport.

Use UI Automator/ADB for Android system UI; use Godot state assertions and injected touch for the canvas. Do not assume Godot's drawn buttons are Android accessibility widgets. Do not add notification/permission test requirements for features the Android client does not implement.

Markdown source
# System Ui

Runtime: Android. Emulator or physical device.

Report PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with evidence. This procedure needs recorded LLM/manual execution. The automated APK cases cover shared client logic, English Gboard input and basic lifecycle, but do not establish this additional coverage as passing.

1. Use an isolated connection, with terminal output and a deliberately displayed Graffitty messages panel.
2. Copy terminal/message text through the client's available copy action, then paste into another Android app. Copy English, Korean, emoji, and multiline text from that app and paste into the focused terminal. Check exact server text.
3. Exercise Android Back with a client dialog and with the system keyboard open; verify only the intended layer closes.
4. Exercise any supported external-link or log-opening action through the Android intent resolver. A desktop shell-open call is not evidence for this boundary.
5. Exercise Android split-screen and lock/unlock, including with the keyboard visible. Verify controls avoid actual status/navigation bars, display cutouts, and keyboard insets in portrait and landscape.
6. On a test environment configured for the supported network path, interrupt and restore Android connectivity while connected. Verify the reconnect path and server session continuity. If testing Tailscale, exercise the actual Android VPN app; a local loopback server only validates the transport.

Use UI Automator/ADB for Android system UI; use Godot state assertions and injected touch for the canvas. Do not assume Godot's drawn buttons are Android accessibility widgets. Do not add notification/permission test requirements for features the Android client does not implement.

android-touch-menus

Keep Android menus compact, scroll without activating or highlighting commands, and preserve submenu and Back behavior.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Android compact touch menus — UI-05

Use the existing Android runtime harness with a disposable app/server fixture. Open the floating menu and View using touchscreen events. The menu must stay at most 320×360 logical pixels, clamped further to the available keyboard-safe viewport, rather than filling the screen. Scroll across rows repeatedly: content must move, all pressed highlights must clear, and release must neither execute a command nor dismiss the menu. Reach the final item, dismiss via the shared Android Back policy, reopen, toggle the opener, and enter/leave a real submenu. A flick keeps the rows gliding after the finger lifts; touching the gliding menu stops it without running a command (GE-09). The original server terminal must survive and no workspace contacts may remain.

Unchecked options must show a legible empty outline on the dark menu, including before touch or keyboard focus. Radio choices use circles, checkbox options use squares, and checked/disabled states remain distinct. Toggle an option in a menu that stays open: its indicator must update without shifting the label or replacing the command icon. Ordinary commands must not gain checkbox indicators.

The automated case injects touch events through Godot's real input routing, including emulated mouse copies. It runs both in desktop simulation and in an APK. It does not claim human finger smoothness, physical Back-gesture delivery, real IME cycles, or phone/foldable rotation coverage. Supplement on both geometries with physical scrolling, cancellation, long translated labels, keyboard open/close, context menus and selecting the final command. tests/touch_menu_smoke.gd covers 1.5× scaling, cancellation, extra fingers, command identity, keyboard insets and checked/unchecked/radio/disabled indicators in menus that stay open.

LLM suite specification

Touch controls and terminal title masking

Connect to a Mac server, then a Windows or Linux server. The accessory keyboard always offers Esc, Ctrl, Alt, Tab, Shift and arrows; it never requires Command or Option. Open Shell, Edit, View and Sessions. Verify New Tab, New Chromium, new panes, Close Pane, Copy, Paste, Find, Overview, Fit to Pane and Messages are available. Use an external keyboard: Ctrl+Shift+C/V copy/paste while plain Ctrl+C still interrupts the terminal. Activate a new pane through the menu.

Run a terminal application with a status line at the bottom. Zoom out until the title grows over the top rows and the icons disappear, then zoom back in. The terminal content must not shift or shrink. Its last row stays visible, the grid size stays unchanged, and only the top rows are covered by the title. Inspect actual rendered pixels, not just visibility flags. Repeat with the keyboard open.

The automated shared scenario checks menu coverage, modifier hints, unchanged terminal geometry/grid, and rendered coloured text on the bottom row across zooms.

direct-touch

Direct targeting, pane and wire dragging, title fit, anchored pinch, and continuous pan through finger lift/rejoin

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Direct touch navigation

There is no center pointer. Touch titles, buttons, and node sockets directly. Drag a title to move its pane and an output socket to an input to connect nodes. Double-tap a title to fit. Long press opens the context action. Two-finger pinch and pan keep the existing stationary and moving finger anchors. Releasing or canceling touch must release all captured buttons and preserve the terminal grid.

Terminal content scrolls with one finger by default; double-tap-and-drag selects. Use View → Terminal Touch Scrolling to switch between One Finger and Three Fingers. The latter permits ordinary one-finger selection. In both modes, adding a second finger cancels any pending selection and starts pinch navigation without copying.

After two-finger panning starts, lift either finger and keep moving the remaining finger: the canvas must continue following it at unchanged zoom. Holding that finger must not select text, drag a pane, click or open a long-press menu. Put a second finger down again (including a new touch ID): neither contact change may jump the camera, and two-finger pan/pinch must resume immediately using the new contact positions. Repeat the lift/rejoin cycle, then lift both fingers and verify an ordinary one-finger tap works again. Keep the initial pinch/three-finger scroll guard: an uncommitted gesture must not leak movement into the workspace, and lifting fingers after three-finger scrolling must not become panning.

Header actions use the phone's own fit scale and compact desktop spacing. Hidden actions release the entire title width. Test both above and below the half-fit visibility threshold. The shared runtime scenario also checks cursor shape and typing navigation; the actual APK adds native IME and Flat 2D assertions. See mac-trackpad for the separate Mac intent cases.

scrollbar-interactions

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Terminal scrollbar interactions

Run in Flat 2D, including with touch controls enabled. Create enough shell output to fill several pages of history, then start halfway through it.

  1. Drag the thumb upward and downward. The terminal history must follow it.
  2. Click empty track above the thumb, then below it. Each click pages in the requested direction.
  3. Press and hold empty track above and below the thumb. After a short initial delay, paging repeats until the thumb reaches the pointer.
  4. Move outside the scrollbar and release. Scrolling must stop and stay stopped.
  5. The world must retain its pan and zoom. No scrollbar press may reach terminal text-selection input. Any script or engine error fails the test.

The replay uses actual viewport mouse events and native terminal history. Its hold durations use real elapsed time, even when other replay pacing is disabled.

tab-close-touch

Touch tab closes retain widths for two seconds, then expand smoothly.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Crowded tab labels and continuous add/remove animations

With enough room for a number and close button, the active tab shows both. Hovering an inactive tab shows its close button beside its number. With room only for the number, every tab keeps its number, including tabs with empty or one-character titles. Only the active tab replaces its number with close when the pointer is directly over the number. Leaving restores the number. Clicking an inactive number selects that tab without closing it.

With ample room, add a second tab using the plus button. The first tab must keep its bounds; the new tab opens to its right, never over its close button. The new tab and plus hit target stay separated throughout the animation, including when another tab is added before the preceding insertion finishes.

Add a tab to a crowded strip using the plus button. The new tab starts narrow outside the preceding tab's edge and grows while the other tabs shrink and move left. Close the last tab: it shrinks away outside the preceding tab while surviving tabs grow and their right edges move right. With ample room, surviving tabs stay fixed. The closing label retains its normal content insets; it must not jump left or slide over a neighbour's close button. The viewport must retain the closing view until it finishes shrinking, and the plus hit target stays outside it. Verify trailing, middle, adjacent simultaneous and rapid repeated closes, and interrupt insertion with closure and closure with insertion. Both transitions must have intermediate rendered bounds, without snapping widths or restarting on ordinary owner updates. Adding another tab during an animation continues from the current bounds. The plus button follows the changing trailing edge smoothly when tabs have already reached their maximum width.

The reference is Chromium's TabContainer, BoundsAnimator, and Tween: 200 ms quadratic ease-out over complete bounds, narrow insertion at the preceding edge, and deletion after the closing animation. Chromium subtracts its decorative tab overlap in StartInsertTabAnimation and GetTargetBoundsForClosingTab; Graffitty uses a positive 3 px gap instead, so that subtraction must not be copied onto its content bounds. Closing content collapses to zero at the preceding edge, with its label insets preserved inside a clipping view. GetMidAnimationTrailingX keeps Chromium's closing tabs inside the viewport; Graffitty likewise retains the animated extent instead of clipping immediately to the final tab count. Chromium's Tab::UpdateIconVisibility also hides the close control below the minimum tab width; a collapsed insertion must not expose a close hit target outside its own tab.

Repeated mouse closes of non-trailing tabs hold widths so the next close button stays under the pointer. Moving up to 40 logical pixels below or 60 pixels right of the strip keeps that mode. Leaving further waits 300 ms before animated expansion; returning before the deadline cancels it. An outside press releases it immediately. Touch closes wait two seconds (postponed during a drag). Trailing closes permit immediate expansion. Keyboard closes do not enter closing mode. Inserting a tab releases the constraint. The first tab and hidden initial layout do not animate.

Record per-frame bounds during actual plus/close clicks against a private session server. Capture both compact label widths and the selected hover state.

With enough room for a number and close button, the active tab shows both.
Hovering an inactive tab shows its close button beside its number. With room
only for the number, every tab keeps its number, including tabs with empty or
one-character titles. Only the active tab replaces its number with close when
the pointer is directly over the number. Leaving restores the number. Clicking
an inactive number selects that tab without closing it.

With ample room, add a second tab using the plus button. The first tab must
keep its bounds; the new tab opens to its right, never over its close button.
The new tab and plus hit target stay separated throughout the animation,
including when another tab is added before the preceding insertion finishes.

Add a tab to a crowded strip using the plus button. The new tab starts narrow
outside the preceding tab's edge and grows while the other tabs shrink and move
left. Close the last tab: it shrinks away outside the preceding tab while
surviving tabs grow and their right edges move right. With ample room, surviving
tabs stay fixed. The closing label retains its normal content insets; it must
not jump left or slide over a neighbour's close button. The viewport must retain
the closing view until it finishes shrinking, and the plus hit target stays
outside it. Verify trailing, middle, adjacent simultaneous and rapid repeated
closes, and interrupt insertion with closure and closure with insertion.
Both transitions must have intermediate rendered bounds, without snapping widths
or restarting on ordinary owner updates.
Adding another tab during an animation continues from the current bounds.
The plus button follows the changing trailing edge smoothly when tabs have
already reached their maximum width.

The reference is Chromium's
[TabContainer](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/chrome/browser/ui/views/tabs/tab_container.cc),
[BoundsAnimator](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/ui/views/animation/bounds_animator.h),
and [Tween](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/ui/gfx/animation/tween.cc):
200 ms quadratic ease-out over complete bounds, narrow insertion at the
preceding edge, and deletion after the closing animation. Chromium subtracts
its decorative tab overlap in `StartInsertTabAnimation` and
`GetTargetBoundsForClosingTab`; Graffitty uses a positive 3 px gap instead, so
that subtraction must not be copied onto its content bounds. Closing content

a clipping view. `GetMidAnimationTrailingX` keeps Chromium's closing tabs inside
the viewport; Graffitty likewise retains the animated extent instead of clipping
immediately to the final tab count. Chromium's [`Tab::UpdateIconVisibility`](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/chrome/browser/ui/views/tabs/tab.cc)
also hides the close control below the minimum tab width; a collapsed insertion
must not expose a close hit target outside its own tab.

Repeated mouse closes of non-trailing tabs hold widths so the next close button
stays under the pointer. Moving up to 40 logical pixels below or 60 pixels right
of the strip keeps that mode. Leaving further waits 300 ms before animated
expansion; returning before the deadline cancels it. An outside press releases
it immediately. Touch closes wait two seconds (postponed during a drag).

night-lighting-tab-flight

The baked Bistro's fixtures illuminate readable scenery at all nine sessions, and session flights, interruptions, and saved-view returns land without a late directional flick or abrupt stop.

✅ pass · 69.6 s · AV1 · 2026-09-28T17:44+09:00

LLM suite specification

Bistro night lighting and session-flight landings

Open the baked Bistro

Open nine shell sessions and select the installed bistro world. Use the actual application, with its default terminal effects and saved per-session framing.

Inspect every destination

Click sessions 1 through 9 in order. At each stop, inspect the ground, walls, and furniture/foliage, especially sessions 7–9. Fixtures should illuminate nearby surfaces; merely increasing exposure or a uniform fill does not prove this. Unlit streets must retain a dark night appearance, with warm local pools of light; daylight-like blanket fill fails. There should be no giant glowing rectangles, clipped scenery, or black voids. Save scenery-only and full-window captures, recording any remaining defects.

Watch continuous flights

Record the actual session clicks and the entire motion. Include the street/cafe entrance, the outdoor destinations, and the long return from 9 to 1. Examine frames through the last quarter and the final landing. The camera should slow gradually, without a late sideways flick, abrupt turn, stop-and-restart, or cut. Check actual displayed position, orientation, and lens as supporting evidence; a smooth endpoint or a passing scripted check alone is insufficient.

Interrupt and revisit

Click a different session during a flight, then let it land. Pinch one session to 1.2x, visit another, and return. Both the interruption and return should be continuous, with the saved framing restored. Report PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with the recording, lighting captures, and frame/route telemetry. A rendered capture is required for lighting; do not claim a headless run establishes visual quality.

Resize during a flight

Start another session flight and resize the application to a taller aspect ratio while it moves. The camera must keep moving continuously and land at the new framing, without snapping to a different lens at the end. Record the resize and at least one second after arrival.

Markdown source
# Bistro night lighting and session-flight landings

## Open the baked Bistro

Open nine shell sessions and select the installed `bistro` world. Use the actual
application, with its default terminal effects and saved per-session framing.

## Inspect every destination

Click sessions 1 through 9 in order. At each stop, inspect the ground, walls, and
furniture/foliage, especially sessions 7–9. Fixtures should illuminate nearby
surfaces; merely increasing exposure or a uniform fill does not prove this.
Unlit streets must retain a dark night appearance, with warm local pools of
light; daylight-like blanket fill fails. There should be no giant glowing rectangles, clipped scenery, or black voids.
Save scenery-only and full-window captures, recording any remaining defects.

## Watch continuous flights

Record the actual session clicks and the entire motion. Include the street/cafe
entrance, the outdoor destinations, and the long return from 9 to 1. Examine
frames through the last quarter and the final landing. The camera should slow
gradually, without a late sideways flick, abrupt turn, stop-and-restart, or cut.
Check actual displayed position, orientation, and lens as supporting evidence;
a smooth endpoint or a passing scripted check alone is insufficient.

## Interrupt and revisit

Click a different session during a flight, then let it land. Pinch one session to 1.2x,
visit another, and return. Both the interruption and return should be continuous,
with the saved framing restored. Report PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with the recording,
lighting captures, and frame/route telemetry. A rendered capture is required for
lighting; do not claim a headless run establishes visual quality.

## Resize during a flight

Start another session flight and resize the application to a taller aspect ratio
while it moves. The camera must keep moving continuously and land at the new
framing, without snapping to a different lens at the end. Record the resize and
at least one second after arrival.

overview-pane-resources

Bistro terminal backdrops are 85% opaque; zoomed-out panes replace hidden toolbar controls with readable live PID, CPU and RAM summaries.

✅ pass · 17.2 s · AV1 · 2026-10-04T16:58+09:00

LLM suite specification

Overview pane resources

  1. Open View → World → Bistro. Create three terminal panes in one tab.
  2. At normal zoom, confirm terminal backdrops are 85% opaque and text is readable against the scenery.
  3. Zoom out until resource monitor and other toolbar buttons disappear.
  4. Every visible pane has its original unchanged header, with a separate narrow multiline screen-space panel above it: stable pane UID (%N), process-tree CPU percentage and RAM (M/G, binary units). The pane UID is on the first line; CPU and RAM occupy separate rows with aligned icon and value columns. The panel does not repeat the title. A chip SVG and a memory-module SVG replace the CPU and RAM words. Panels prefer above the top-left corner, then slide along the pane edges to stay visible. They never cover any terminal content, headers, or other stats, and have no connector lines. If no free on-screen edge space exists, hide the stats rather than cover stdout. Pan the panes near the top edge and verify the stats move beside or below them. They do not intercept clicks.
  5. Wait for live samples. Each UID identifies its own pane, including unfocused panes. Run a short CPU workload in one shell and confirm that pane's CPU reading updates. Pending/unavailable/paused data shows a dash, not a fabricated zero.
  6. Zoom back in. The captions disappear and full toolbar controls return. Repeat zooming out; captions return with current stats. Shells and pane sizes are preserved.
Markdown source
# Overview pane resources

1. Open View → World → Bistro. Create three terminal panes in one tab.
2. At normal zoom, confirm terminal backdrops are 85% opaque and text is readable against the scenery.
3. Zoom out until resource monitor and other toolbar buttons disappear.
4. Every visible pane has its original unchanged header, with a separate narrow multiline screen-space panel above it: stable pane UID (`%N`), process-tree CPU percentage and RAM (M/G, binary units). The pane UID is on the first line; CPU and RAM occupy separate rows with aligned icon and value columns. The panel does not repeat the title. A chip SVG and a memory-module SVG replace the CPU and RAM words. Panels prefer above the top-left corner, then slide along the pane edges to stay visible. They never cover any terminal content, headers, or other stats, and have no connector lines. If no free on-screen edge space exists, hide the stats rather than cover stdout. Pan the panes near the top edge and verify the stats move beside or below them. They do not intercept clicks.
5. Wait for live samples. Each UID identifies its own pane, including unfocused panes. Run a short CPU workload in one shell and confirm that pane's CPU reading updates. Pending/unavailable/paused data shows a dash, not a fabricated zero.
6. Zoom back in. The captions disappear and full toolbar controls return. Repeat zooming out; captions return with current stats. Shells and pane sizes are preserved.

pinch-zoom-tab-flight

In Bistro, after a pinch zoom, switching tabs flies to the next wall in one continuous motion and lands without a jump cut, restoring each destination tab's own zoom.

✅ pass · 37.1 s · AV1 · 2026-11-17T22:19+09:00

LLM suite specification

A pinch zoom survives a tab flight without a jump cut

Regression: after a pinch zoom, the flight to another wall looked wrong and its last frame jumped to a different framing.

Open Bistro

  1. Launch from the repository root:

    mise run dev -- --shell=/bin/sh --tabs=1

  2. Choose View > World > Bistro and wait for the camera to land. If the item is missing, report BLOCKED: the Bistro world is not installed.

  3. Create the second tab. It must keep Bistro without reloading the world or switching to Flat.

Pinch zoom a little

  1. Over the terminal, pinch outward on the trackpad once, gently: about a quarter more zoom. Do not type.
  2. Expected: the view zooms in smoothly and stays there.

Switch tabs and watch the flight

  1. Record the screen, then click the second tab in the tab bar.
  2. Expected: the camera leaves the first wall and flies to the second in one continuous motion. Nothing snaps back to an unzoomed view on the way.
  3. Expected: when it lands, the second tab retains its own original framing, without a final jump. Arrival overlaps departure; camera and scatter ease together through the final 500 ms and stop together. The first tab's pinch must not change the second tab.
  4. Fill both terminals with coloured text and repeat. The terminal planes, pane backings and borders stay at their world locations as the camera leaves one wall and approaches the next. They must not travel with the camera like a screen overlay. Letters scatter from and settle onto those anchored planes. embedded-input

Desktop Chromium accepts clicks, typing, selection and scrolling inside its GPU pane

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Open the deterministic chromium fixture in the desktop workspace. Through the actual window input route, click its button, type in the input, drag across the paragraph to select text, right-click, and scroll. Assert DOM results and a live GPU frame. No gesture may call the chromium input API or DOM click/selection/scroll APIs. Run with --headful: AppKit native menu tracking can block while the background window guard suppresses its window. A hidden-window run cannot certify native menu keyboard navigation. The native Chrome window must remain closed. Repeat after changing pane size to catch page-coordinate versus GPU backing-pixel mistakes.

Scroll to the document bottom. Discrete wheel ticks must leave page pixels stable. On macOS with the Chrome-style backend, a continuous native trackpad gesture must visibly stretch the page in one direction, without repeatedly snapping back while input continues. After release, the page must spring back and settle at its original pixel position. Its document scroll position must remain at the bottom. Exercise this in the normal desktop CEF path. Include tiny fractional horizontal noise in the vertical gesture: the page must stay visible throughout the bounce, without sliding away sideways. The native macOS rubber-band stretch is NOT_APPLICABLE on Windows/Linux, where Chromium disables elastic overscroll, and on the windowless Alloy backend. Alloy cannot deliver AppKit scroll phases: CDP ends every wheel event immediately, which restarted the spring per trackpad sample and ignored slow motion. Alloy wheels use CEF's windowless wheel instead, whose synthetic phases stop at the edge. Still send continuous scrolling with fractional horizontal noise and require stable visible pixels and unchanged bottom scroll position. Clicks, selection, typing, native menus and verified GPU imports remain mandatory on every desktop platform.

Allow the default context menu on the input. Right-click it and check that the Godot menu opens at the clicked point. Use actual keyboard navigation to select Chromium's Select All command and verify the input selection. A page handler that prevents the default menu must continue to suppress it.

   ```sh
     --config=tests/llm-e2e/suites/godot/flat-world/camera-zoom-tab-switch.conf
   ```

2. Confirm two terminal tabs are open and the camera is idle.

## Type and switch while zoomed

1. Type in the first tab until the camera zooms in.
2. While zoomed in, click the second tab.
3. Stop typing and watch the animation finish.

## Verify animation continuity

1. Confirm the second tab is active.
2. Confirm the camera moves smoothly while glyphs leave and the backing recedes.
3. Confirm the camera eases to the destination while it builds, without jump-cutting or freezing during that movement.
4. Repeat with dense text in both tabs, typing zoom around 1.8, camera tilt of
   12 degrees, depth-of-field blur, and the Mild preset's purple defocus tint.
   Print repeated alphabet/number rows so blur and brightness are measurable.
5. For Godot, run the Push/Pull tab transition in both directions (to a later
   and to an earlier tab). The fixture selects the fixed typing zoom with
   `zoom_mode = "typing"`; adaptive framing is the default.
   Other frontends must exercise their supported Scatter
   transitions. Review consecutive rendered
   frames at departure and arrival. Switching from live text to captured pieces
   must preserve blur, color, brightness, and antialiased glyph coverage. The
   retained full-pane capture can resample a cropped live texture: the dense
   fixture permits under 2% mean absolute RGB error, while separately requiring
   mean-color distance below 0.005 and edge-energy change below 12%.
   The following one or two frames must not suddenly sharpen or brighten the text.
   Blur may ease away during flight; it must not jump when the camera's typing
   zoom resets. Replacing assembled pieces with live text must also match.
6. Retain all rendered flight frames and lens telemetry. The Godot replay prints
   `ZOOM_APPEARANCE_EVIDENCE` directories containing a 60 Hz frame sequence and
   `lens.json`. Coordinate-only or headless results cannot certify appearance.
Replay checks
  • Typing zooms the camera in (2.50x)
  • The second tab is active
  • Through the switch and back to idle: no jump cut
  • It never freezes while zoomed (0 frames still)
  • It eases back to idle (1.00x at the end)

# One camera for the world and every window

## Prepare two windows in one tab

1. Launch from the repository root:

   ```sh
   mise run dev -- --world=color --bg=#101822 --shell=/bin/sh --tabs=2
   ```

   Configure the fixed typing zoom first (adaptive framing is the default):
   `[effects.camera]` with `zoom_mode = "typing"` and `zoom = 1.15`.

2. In the first tab run `printf '\033]0;ALPHA\007'; clear; echo ALPHA`, in the
   second the same with `BRAVO`.
3. Merge BRAVO into ALPHA: drag BRAVO's tab onto the middle of ALPHA's tab,
   hold until ALPHA's content shows, move down into it and release. If that
   fails, report BLOCKED and refer to `tabs-and-panes/tab-hover-merge`.
4. Drag the windows by their headers so both are fully visible side by side.
   Take a screenshot at rest.

## Type and watch the camera

1. Start a screen recording. Click inside BRAVO and type steadily for three
   seconds.
2. Expected: the whole workspace, both windows and the background, zooms
   toward BRAVO's cursor as one scene. ALPHA moves and scales with it; it does
   not stay fixed while only BRAVO's content zooms.
3. Expected: the view leans gently toward the cursor's side, without
   wide-angle stretching. ALPHA and the far side soften and darken slightly;
   text around the cursor stays sharp. The tab bar never moves.

## Interact while zoomed

1. Type a few more characters in BRAVO, then immediately click inside the
   visible part of ALPHA.
2. Expected: ALPHA takes the keyboard (typed text appears in ALPHA) and the
   camera glides to ALPHA's cursor, without cutting to another view.
   Keep docked panels visible: cursor containment at their boundaries must
   follow the eased cursor during the focus change instead of snapping the camera.
3. Pinch on the trackpad over empty background. Expected: the whole scene
   zooms, not a single window.

## Verify rest

1. Stop typing and wait three seconds.
2. Expected: the camera eases back, and both windows return exactly to their
   arranged places, sharp and evenly lit. Compare with the rest screenshot.
3. Report PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED with the recording and both screenshots.
Replay checks
  • Setup merged both panes into one tab
  • Floating panes settle before capturing the layout
  • BRAVO takes the keyboard and the camera zooms toward it (2.00x)
  • ALPHA moves with the one camera instead of staying put
  • The lean stays within its limit
  • Part of ALPHA is on screen while zoomed
  • ALPHA takes the keyboard: the text typed after the click appears in ALPHA
  • The camera glides to ALPHA's cursor: no jump cut
  • A pinch anywhere zooms the one camera (1.25x)
  • At rest both windows are back exactly where they were arranged (0.00 px off)
