✅ pass · 144.6 s · AV1 · 2026-09-28T01:51+09:00

LLM suite specification

Tab flights restore each space's camera view

Launch mise run dev -- --world=color --shell=/bin/sh --config=tests/llm-e2e/suites/godot/flat-world/per-tab-camera-view.conf. Keep the window size fixed. This fixture makes typing and idle zoom equal so transient typing effects cannot masquerade as remembered navigation zoom. Record continuous video of switches and capture settled reference screenshots. Report PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with evidence; idle screenshots alone cannot prove a correct animation destination.

Prepare distinct views

Create tabs ALPHA, BETA, and GAMMA. Turn off View → Floating Pane Physics in each so collision responses cannot change the reference placements. In each, create two terminals, print unique markers and echo $$, and arrange them differently. Use pinch zoom and right-button dragging to set ALPHA to a close view panned right and up, with an off-center terminal prominent in view. Set BETA to a wider view panned left and down. Leave GAMMA at View → Fit to Main Area. Do not move panes to simulate camera navigation.

After gestures settle, capture a reference for each tab showing the pane corners, text scale, and main-area border where visible. Record navigation zoom and pan when observable, in addition to screenshots. The three references must be visibly distinct in both scale and framing. Wait for each view to settle before leaving it.

Restore the destination during the flight

Switch ALPHA → BETA → GAMMA → ALPHA, then reverse the sequence. For every switch, the animation must finish at the destination tab's own last settled zoom and pan. It must not inherit the source tab's framing, fit all panes, or reset to Main Area. Once settled, pane corners and text scale must match that destination's reference (allow at most two screen pixels of rasterization rounding).

Inspect the recording through the landing and for at least one second afterward. The flight must approach the remembered destination directly and continuously, with no intermediate landing at a default view followed by a second pan/zoom, snap, or corrective jump. Tabs must remain interactive afterward: click a visible terminal and type a marker without an unexpected camera reset.

Update one remembered view

In BETA, change both zoom and horizontal/vertical pan to a new, clearly different view. Wait for gestures to settle and capture a new reference. Visit ALPHA and GAMMA: their original references must still match. Return to BETA: only its new reference must match, including the flight's destination. Repeat the round trip twice to detect accumulated drift or a saved view being overwritten on tab entry.

Interrupt switches and reset one tab

Start ALPHA → BETA and click GAMMA before the flight finishes. After landing, GAMMA must match its saved Main Area view. Return to ALPHA and BETA: both must retain their last settled references; an intermediate animation frame must not overwrite either saved view. Repeat with BETA → ALPHA interrupted by BETA and verify BETA returns to its own latest view without a jump.

In BETA, choose View → Fit to Main Area, let it settle, and capture that reset view. Switch away and return: BETA must now remember Main Area, while ALPHA keeps its custom zoom and pan. Verify pane placements, tab membership, and original shell PIDs are unchanged by all navigation and switches.

# Tab flights restore each space's camera view

Launch `mise run dev -- --world=color --shell=/bin/sh --config=tests/llm-e2e/suites/godot/flat-world/per-tab-camera-view.conf`. Keep the window size fixed. This fixture makes typing and idle zoom equal so transient typing effects cannot masquerade as remembered navigation zoom. Record continuous video of switches and capture settled reference screenshots. Report PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with evidence; idle screenshots alone cannot prove a correct animation destination.

## Prepare distinct views

Create tabs ALPHA, BETA, and GAMMA. Turn off **View → Floating Pane Physics** in each so collision responses cannot change the reference placements. In each, create two terminals, print unique markers and `echo $$`, and arrange them differently. Use pinch zoom and right-button dragging to set ALPHA to a close view panned right and up, with an off-center terminal prominent in view. Set BETA to a wider view panned left and down. Leave GAMMA at **View → Fit to Main Area**. Do not move panes to simulate camera navigation.

After gestures settle, capture a reference for each tab showing the pane corners, text scale, and main-area border where visible. Record navigation zoom and pan when observable, in addition to screenshots. The three references must be visibly distinct in both scale and framing. Wait for each view to settle before leaving it.

## Restore the destination during the flight

Switch ALPHA → BETA → GAMMA → ALPHA, then reverse the sequence. For every switch, the animation must finish at the destination tab's own last settled zoom and pan. It must not inherit the source tab's framing, fit all panes, or reset to Main Area. Once settled, pane corners and text scale must match that destination's reference (allow at most two screen pixels of rasterization rounding).

Inspect the recording through the landing and for at least one second afterward. The flight must approach the remembered destination directly and continuously, with no intermediate landing at a default view followed by a second pan/zoom, snap, or corrective jump. Tabs must remain interactive afterward: click a visible terminal and type a marker without an unexpected camera reset.

## Update one remembered view

In BETA, change both zoom and horizontal/vertical pan to a new, clearly different view. Wait for gestures to settle and capture a new reference. Visit ALPHA and GAMMA: their original references must still match. Return to BETA: only its new reference must match, including the flight's destination. Repeat the round trip twice to detect accumulated drift or a saved view being overwritten on tab entry.

## Interrupt switches and reset one tab

Start ALPHA → BETA and click GAMMA before the flight finishes. After landing, GAMMA must match its saved Main Area view. Return to ALPHA and BETA: both must retain their last settled references; an intermediate animation frame must not overwrite either saved view. Repeat with BETA → ALPHA interrupted by BETA and verify BETA returns to its own latest view without a jump.

In BETA, choose **View → Fit to Main Area**, let it settle, and capture that reset view. Switch away and return: BETA must now remember Main Area, while ALPHA keeps its custom zoom and pan. Verify pane placements, tab membership, and original shell PIDs are unchanged by all navigation and switches.

render-on-demand

A static workspace stops rendering; terminal output, input, cursor blinking, chromium GPU frames, and animations wake the complete composition promptly, then allow it to sleep again, with rendering capped at 60 FPS.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Workspace rendering on demand

Run the actual application in a window with an isolated configuration and state directory. Use one terminal, default Flat world settings, and a temporary chromium profile. Report PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with evidence. Headless rendering cannot establish pixel updates or GPU-idle behavior. If the native chromium host is unavailable, mark its stage BLOCKED and still complete the terminal and animation stages.

Keep the test window foreground and leave physical keyboard and pointer input idle during automated samples. Concurrent desktop interaction can enter text into the test terminal or pause foreground effects. Do not leave an animated test overlay, live FPS counter, or other diagnostic UI running during idle samples: it would itself request redraws. Measure completed render frames with an in-memory counter, then print the result after each sample. Record continuous motion during animation checks separately. CPU percentage is supporting evidence, not a portable pass/fail threshold or a measurement of watts.

Idle and terminal wake-up

Disable cursor blinking and wait for startup and typing effects to settle. With no moving pointer, chromium, animation, or terminal output, observe a quiet interval of at least one second. There must be no sustained frame loop; incidental OS invalidations are acceptable, but a continuous 30/60 FPS stream is a failure. The terminal session must remain alive.

Arrange delayed terminal output, then leave the workspace idle. The new text must appear without moving the pointer, pressing another key, or resizing the window. Verify both terminal text and the final composited window pixels change. Confirm it returns to idle after the output and effects settle. Enable cursor blinking: the cursor must visibly blink, waking only the necessary frames. Disable blinking again and verify idle rendering resumes.

Input, navigation, and effects

Type into the focused terminal. Echo and typing effects must become visible promptly. Open and dismiss a menu; hover a pane button. These UI changes must appear even after a long idle interval. Pan and zoom, then press Command+Enter to fit the pane and again to restore the previous view. Both animations must show intermediate frames, end at their intended framing, and stop producing frames after settling.

Repeat with typing sparks/ripples enabled. Observe the effect while active and after its final particle has disappeared. A shader clock, an empty particle pool, or repeated unchanged style updates must not keep rendering alive. While content is active, rendering must be capped at 60 FPS. Losing and regaining window focus and switching worlds must not remove the cap; the existing 30 FPS background limit may remain.

Allow the configured adaptive camera ease to settle before the idle sample: the typing idle delay, leave duration, and three times the longer adaptive zoom duration. The subsequent one-second idle interval still allows at most two incidental redraws. The projection must finish exactly rather than keep rewriting depth values with an imperceptible interpolation tail.

Chromium GPU frames

Open a local or data-URL page with a solid red body in an embedded chromium pane using a temporary profile. Wait until it is visible and settled. Without terminal input or pointer motion, change the page to solid blue using a timer or chromium automation. Confirm the chromium's received GPU frame count advances and the final application window visibly changes from red to blue. A received texture with frozen final window pixels is a failure.

Start a page animation that changes its color or counter several times per second. Observe several distinct page frames in the embedded pane while leaving terminal input idle. Stop the animation, close the chromium pane, wait for layout/effects to settle, and confirm the terminal workspace returns to idle rendering. Chromium closure must not leave an always-redrawing compositor or break the remaining terminal.

Automated replay: replays/render-on-demand.gd. It reuses tests/workspace_render_updates_smoke.gd for deterministic idle, terminal, cursor, and animation checks, and adds real Chromium GPU-frame and final-pixel checks. Its screenshot helper makes the dashboard run it windowed. The lower-level smoke test remains runnable without the chromium host.

scrollbar-interactions

Drag the terminal scrollbar, page by clicking empty track, and repeat paging while held without moving the world or selecting text.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Terminal scrollbar interactions

Run in Flat 2D, including with touch controls enabled. Create enough shell output to fill several pages of history, then start halfway through it.

  1. Drag the thumb upward and downward. The terminal history must follow it.
  2. Click empty track above the thumb, then below it. Each click pages in the requested direction.
  3. Press and hold empty track above and below the thumb. After a short initial delay, paging repeats until the thumb reaches the pointer.
  4. Move outside the scrollbar and release. Scrolling must stop and stay stopped.
  5. The world must retain its pan and zoom. No scrollbar press may reach terminal text-selection input. Any script or engine error fails the test.

The replay uses actual viewport mouse events and native terminal history. Its hold durations use real elapsed time, even when other replay pacing is disabled.

# Terminal scrollbar interactions

Run in Flat 2D, including with touch controls enabled. Create enough shell
output to fill several pages of history, then start halfway through it.

1. Drag the thumb upward and downward. The terminal history must follow it.
2. Click empty track above the thumb, then below it. Each click pages in the

3. Press and hold empty track above and below the thumb. After a short initial
   delay, paging repeats until the thumb reaches the pointer.
4. Move outside the scrollbar and release. Scrolling must stop and stay stopped.
5. The world must retain its pan and zoom. No scrollbar press may reach terminal

The replay uses actual viewport mouse events and native terminal history. Its

Status strips share camera effects

Status strips are painted on the same sheet as their panes. Their readable size, visibility and perimeter placement depend on deliberate zoom/pan and pane layout. Typing zoom, follow, tilt, drift and depth of field transform the baked result.

  1. In Flat, zoom out to about 45% until a resource strip appears. Confirm that its text is readable and its panel is outside terminal content.

  4. Freeze a tilted frame and compare rendered status glyphs with the depth-of-field compositor enabled and disabled at the identical pose. Preserve both images; a numeric blur setting alone does not establish that the strip was blurred.
  5. Pan and change manual zoom. Placement and readable scale must update for the new framing, keeping terminal content clear. Main View hides overview strips.
  6. Repeat zoom/pan and typing checks in Flat 2D. Tab-transition captures must use the strip's sheet extent and must not apply its compensating scale twice.

# Status strips share camera effects

Status strips are painted on the same sheet as their panes. Their readable size,
visibility and perimeter placement depend on deliberate zoom/pan and pane layout.
Typing zoom, follow, tilt, drift and depth of field transform the baked result.

1. In Flat, zoom out to about 45% until a resource strip appears. Confirm that
   its text is readable and its panel is outside terminal content.
2. Type with zoom and tilt enabled. The strip must move, scale and tilt with the
   sheet, including perspective and depth-of-field blur. It must not jump to a
   different pane edge, keep itself upright or toggle visibility as effects run.
3. Check that the strip's sheet transform and layout-rebuild count stay unchanged
   throughout the temporary camera motion. CPU/RAM and agent updates still work.
4. Freeze a tilted frame and compare rendered status glyphs with the depth-of-field
   compositor enabled and disabled at the identical pose. Preserve both images;
   a numeric blur setting alone does not establish that the strip was blurred.
5. Pan and change manual zoom. Placement and readable scale must update for the
   new framing, keeping terminal content clear. Main View hides overview strips.
6. Repeat zoom/pan and typing checks in Flat 2D. Tab-transition captures must use

status-strip-navigation

Plan status placement once per navigation destination and animate around pane edges without learning intermediate positions or jumping at completion.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Status strips during navigation

Use two real tiled panes and the production Main View/pane-fit controls. Run in both Flat and Flat 2D, sampling the actual tween through its completion frame.

  1. Zoom out until status strips appear, and retain their settled placements.
  2. Toggle Main View and back. Strips fade out/in while moving with the camera. They recover the same placements; hidden Main View must not replace them.
  3. Fit a pane and return. Check the same continuity and placement history.
  4. Reverse Main View midway. Start from the displayed geometry and opacity.
  5. Pan toward a viewport edge so a strip must change sides. Its path follows its own pane's outside edges, not a straight line through the pane. Crossing a neighboring pane during this brief animation is permitted.
  6. During each animation, verify that the placement solver does not rerun and remembered positions remain unchanged. Commit only the planned destination.
  7. Check every sampled frame for visible overlap with the owner, abrupt position or opacity changes, and any correction after the tween finishes. Preserve rendered start/middle/end frames of the edge change in each world for review.
  8. Interrupt with manual zoom and verify ordinary navigation resumes.

Placement and path geometry live in graffitty-workspace-core::status_strip. The E2E replay covers the Godot integration; Rust tests also check invalid inputs, all edge-to-edge routes, resizing, and interrupted-path continuity.

status-strip-thresholds

Pane titles keep a constant readable on-screen font size inside their frames; only right-side icons hide at half size, independently of StatusStrip

✅ pass · 31.7 s · AV1 · 2026-10-04T16:58+09:00

LLM suite specification

Readable pane titles at every zoom

The title font must keep the same readable on-screen size while the pane zooms through manual viewpoint changes. Typing zoom and blur still affect the title together with the pane. A constant theme font setting is not enough if the camera shrinks the rendered text. There must be no font-size switch at any zoom threshold.

  1. Start at 100% zoom and note the title's rendered glyph height.
  2. Zoom to 150%, 100%, 67%, just above and below 50%, 40%, and 27%, then back in. The title's rendered glyph height must stay equal to the original, within one screen pixel. Check both directions across 50% for sudden changes.
  3. The title remains attached inside the pane's top edge, with the same alignment. It must not float above or drift away from the frame. Long titles truncate to fit; they do not shrink their font to fit.
  4. The first terminal row stays unobstructed, and the PTY grid does not resize.
  5. Only the right-side action icons disappear below 50%. Their invisible buttons must not intercept clicks. StatusStrip uses its separate, earlier threshold.
  6. Dragging the title, opening its right-click menu, and double-clicking Fit to Pane must continue to work at every zoom level.

Any unexpected error dialog is a failure. This contract supersedes the earlier incorrect expectation that title text should scale down with terminal content.

# Tab animation handoffs preserve the terminal

## Prepare config and tabs

1. Launch from the repository root:

   ```sh
   mise run dev -- --world=color --bg=#101822 --shell=/bin/sh --tabs=2 \
     --config=tests/llm-e2e/suites/godot/flat-world/tab-animation-handoff.conf
   ```

2. In each tab, run `printf 'HANDOFF ALIGNMENT 0123456789\nSECOND LINE 0123456789\n'`.
3. Return to the first tab and wait for the animation to finish.

## Switch tabs

1. Start a screen recording.
2. Click the second tab and let the animation finish.
3. Switch back to the first tab and let the animation finish.

## Verify animation handoffs

1. Review each switch frame by frame.
2. Confirm the text does not disappear or blur for a frame when the animation starts.
3. Confirm the text does not shift by a pixel when it becomes animation pieces.
4. Confirm the text does not shift by a pixel when the animation finishes.
5. Scatter frontends: confirm the leaving window's frame (title bar, buttons,
   border) and its background colour recede and fade first while its text flies
   off, and that the arriving frame and background colour approach from a
   distance and fade in last as the text completes its landing.
6. Godot (Push/Pull): confirm both tabs cross as whole panes, with no separate
   letters or dust. Midway, the leaving frame and text have left their places
   and the arriving ones have not reached theirs.
7. In both, the initial capture must match the live window without a one-frame
   pop, and the fully assembled pieces must be drawn before the live terminal
   replaces them, with no jump or blur at that handoff.

tab-transition

Both Flat renderers push whole panes away and pull the destination in on one shared clock, restoring the destination camera at the same deadline.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Flat tab transition: push, cross, pull

Run in both Flat and Flat 2D (--plugin=flat-2d). Use two tabs with distinct text, multiple panes, an inline image, and different saved pan/zoom. Capture continuous motion; still frames alone do not establish smoothness.

Tab changes use Push/Pull (or none). Letters and dust belong to session switches, not tabs. Before motion starts, retain the outgoing view until the destination's owner snapshot has been repainted and its incoming capture has drawn. Create, close and ordinary switching share this preparation. Loading does not consume any of the transition's 420 ms.

Push the outgoing panes

Switch to a later tab while idle, then while typing has zoomed the camera. The outgoing panes stay whole: text, backgrounds, frames, the active-pane outline, the Main View border, chromium pages and images enlarge together toward the viewer, defocus and fade. Nothing is cut into letters, dust or screenshot-grid shards, and no pane is squeezed or stretched. The camera starts moving immediately, toward the destination tab's saved view.

Cross while the destination arrives

The incoming panes overlap the departure from the first frame: they complete the reciprocal zoom (2x range) and fade in as the outgoing panes fade out. Every pane, border and decoration of both tabs shares one quintic smoothstep clock; saved camera framing must not add a second acceleration. The camera passes through intermediate framing and lands with the panes at the same deadline: there is no settling tail after it. No complete live destination may appear beneath its arriving copy. At completion, replacing the transition with live panes must not jump or flash, and the camera rests on the destination's saved view. Switching to an earlier tab reverses the dolly: outgoing panes shrink away while the incoming ones pull in from in front. Include coloured and dim prompt text (for example, a coloured hostname). Its colour and antialiased edges must match at departure and at the arrival handoff; transition captures must preserve the live terminal's colour space and texel density, including zoomed/cropped panes on the first frame.

Interrupt and preserve sessions

Switch again early in the crossing and late in it. Existing panes retire smoothly, no hidden tab flashes into view, and the camera starts from its displayed frame and lands on the latest tab's saved view. Low frame rates and render stalls keep elapsed transition time. Test an instant switch, disabling tab effects, chromium panes, graph wires and sockets, overview captions, resource strips, and the monitor. Pane layout, shells and content survive.

Replay: replays/tab-transition.gd. Run headless in each renderer for phase, framing and lifecycle checks, then windowed for shader errors and visual review. Set GRAFFITTY_TRANSITION_ARTIFACTS to save representative rendered stages.

Markdown source
# Flat tab transition: push, cross, pull

Run in both Flat and Flat 2D (`--plugin=flat-2d`). Use two tabs with distinct text,
multiple panes, an inline image, and different saved pan/zoom. Capture continuous
motion; still frames alone do not establish smoothness.

Tab changes use **Push/Pull** (or none). Letters and dust belong to session
switches, not tabs. Before motion starts, retain the outgoing view until the
destination's owner snapshot has been repainted and its incoming capture has
drawn. Create, close and ordinary switching share this preparation. Loading does
not consume any of the transition's 420 ms.

## Push the outgoing panes

Switch to a later tab while idle, then while typing has zoomed the camera. The
outgoing panes stay whole: text, backgrounds, frames, the active-pane outline,
the Main View border, chromium pages and images enlarge together toward the
viewer, defocus and fade. Nothing is cut into letters, dust or screenshot-grid
shards, and no pane is squeezed or stretched. The camera starts moving
immediately, toward the destination tab's saved view.

## Cross while the destination arrives

The incoming panes overlap the departure from the first frame: they complete the
reciprocal zoom (2x range) and fade in as the outgoing panes fade out. Every
pane, border and decoration of both tabs shares one quintic smoothstep clock;
saved camera framing must not add a second acceleration. The camera passes
through intermediate framing and lands with the panes at the same deadline:
there is no settling tail after it. No complete live destination may appear
beneath its arriving copy. At completion, replacing the transition with live
panes must not jump or flash, and the camera rests on the destination's saved
view. Switching to an earlier tab reverses the dolly: outgoing panes shrink
away while the incoming ones pull in from in front.
Include coloured and dim prompt text (for example, a coloured hostname). Its
colour and antialiased edges must match at departure and at the arrival handoff;
transition captures must preserve the live terminal's colour space and texel
density, including zoomed/cropped panes on the first frame.

## Interrupt and preserve sessions

Switch again early in the crossing and late in it. Existing panes retire
smoothly, no hidden tab flashes into view, and the camera starts from its
displayed frame and lands on the latest tab's saved view. Low frame rates and
render stalls keep elapsed transition time. Test an instant switch, disabling
tab effects, chromium panes, graph wires and sockets, overview captions, resource
strips, and the monitor. Pane layout, shells and content survive.

Replay: `replays/tab-transition.gd`. Run headless in each renderer for phase,
framing and lifecycle checks, then windowed for shader errors and visual review.
Set `GRAFFITTY_TRANSITION_ARTIFACTS` to save representative rendered stages.

bistro-flight

The real Bistro geometry, fourteen live sessions cycling through authored destinations, saved camera views, and interrupted pane arrival animations remain continuous.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Bistro camera and pane arrival

This specification applies to every required frontend, using the same Bistro assets and authored terminal placements. Run in an isolated test session. The automated driver must inject application actions rather than desktop mouse or keyboard events. Never attach to a personal terminal session.

The Godot adapter captures all fourteen sessions across the nine authored destinations and frame sequences for the 14-to-13 flight and interrupted return, with camera telemetry and live shell identities. Review its PNGs under the isolated cache directory as well as its numeric assertions. On Windows use the interactive desktop renderer.

Open the real Bistro

  1. Start the prototype in offscreen mode and capture the first rendered frame.
  2. Confirm recognizable Bistro streets and buildings and the authored terminal placement. A colored cube or a photograph standing in for Bistro is a failure.
  3. Create fourteen live sessions. Record each pane's session ID and shell PID.
  4. Visit each session and capture its rendered view. Require distinct camera poses within the authored destination list, a visible terminal, and no error diagnostics. After the last authored destination, sessions wrap back to the first destination in order while retaining their own independent shell identities.

Preserve a pinched camera view

  1. At session 1, zoom 1.25 times at an off-center point on the terminal.
  2. Record the world point under the gesture anchor before and after. It stays under the same point unless a documented boundary limits the movement.
  3. Switch to session 2. Record the entire flight at a fixed timestep, with camera pose and viewport telemetry beside every rendered sample.
  4. Session 2 retains its own original view. Returning to session 1 restores session 1's zoom and pan without a last-frame jump. Shell PIDs remain unchanged.

Inspect session 14 to 13 arrival

  1. Select session 14, wait for the view to settle, then select session 13.
  2. Capture the entire transition, including frames immediately before and after the live terminal replaces the incoming transition representation.
  3. The incoming terminal background follows Godot's panel fade while its glyph chunks assemble along their configured paths. The background remains on the terminal sheet; require no added vertical slide or sudden one-frame arrival, even when Bistro geometry crosses it.
  4. Check rendered pixels as well as opacity telemetry. A correct number in a state dump does not establish that a fade is visible.
  5. The title, pane edges, terminal glyphs, and final live surface align on the handoff frame. The bottom visible terminal row remains available.

Interrupt the incoming pane

  1. Begin session 13 to 14. During the incoming fade, select session 13 again.
  2. The outgoing frame begins at the displayed camera pose and opacity. No one-frame disappearance, full-opacity flash, or reset to the old pose.
  3. Let it settle, then type a unique command and confirm actual shell output.
  4. Report PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with the capture directory, state trace, and exact failing frame. A headless logic-only run cannot establish visual PASS.

This specification applies to every required frontend, using the same Bistro
assets and authored terminal placements. Run in an isolated test
session. The automated driver must inject application actions rather than
desktop mouse or keyboard events. Never attach to a personal terminal session.

The Godot adapter captures all fourteen sessions across the nine authored destinations and frame sequences for
the 14-to-13 flight and interrupted return, with camera telemetry and live shell
identities. Review its PNGs under the isolated cache directory as well as its
numeric assertions. On Windows use the interactive desktop renderer.

## Open the real Bistro

1. Start the prototype in offscreen mode and capture the first rendered frame.
2. Confirm recognizable Bistro streets and buildings and the authored terminal placement.
   A colored cube or a photograph standing in for Bistro is a failure.
3. Create fourteen live sessions. Record each pane's session ID and shell PID.
4. Visit each session and capture its rendered view. Require distinct camera poses
   within the authored destination list, a visible terminal, and no error
   diagnostics. After the last authored destination, sessions wrap back to the first
   destination in order while retaining their own independent shell identities.

## Preserve a pinched camera view

1. At session 1, zoom 1.25 times at an off-center point on the terminal.
2. Record the world point under the gesture anchor before and after. It stays
   under the same point unless a documented boundary limits the movement.
3. Switch to session 2. Record the entire flight at a fixed timestep, with camera
   pose and viewport telemetry beside every rendered sample.
4. Session 2 retains its own original view. Returning to session 1 restores session 1's
   zoom and pan without a last-frame jump. Shell PIDs remain unchanged.

## Inspect session 14 to 13 arrival

1. Select session 14, wait for the view to settle, then select session 13.
2. Capture the entire transition, including frames immediately before and
   after the live terminal replaces the incoming transition representation.
3. The incoming terminal background follows Godot's panel fade while its glyph

5. The title, pane edges, terminal glyphs, and final live surface align on the

## Interrupt the incoming pane

desktop-defaults

Local chromium profiles persist actual chromium storage, explicit temporary profiles stay isolated, and private listener controls respect headless startup.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

For Godot on Windows, run python tests/chromium/desktop_defaults_godot_e2e.py --evidence NEW_DIRECTORY from the normal desktop token. Set GRAFFITTY_TEST_SERVER, GRAFFITTY_TEST_GODOT and GRAFFITTY_CHROMIUM_HOST to the frozen executables. This adapter starts a private headless owner and visible Godot frontend, awaits strict IndexedDB transaction completion, closes each original Chromium process, and exercises the actual Sessions remote-access controls. Use only the fixture's temporary profile directories, local HTTP server and loopback listener; only the test-owned native popup receives input. Do not open an existing user's chromium profile.

Require the exact random marker after the actual chromium process closes and reopens with the default profile. The strict IndexedDB commit must run in Chromium through CDP; copying profile files or inspecting preferences is not substitute evidence. Explicit empty profiles must start empty on both creations; an explicit alternate profile must not change the default profile's contents.

Require the declared headless startup to leave its listener closed. Explicit enable must accept loopback connections and disable must stop accepting them, while the original terminal PID survives. This is not acceptance of interactive automatic startup or remote-host profile isolation; those scopes stay separate.

Open persistent-profile-reopened.png and native-view-menu.png. Check that the actual chromium shows the retained PROFILE_… marker and the Sessions controls are readable, without a local profile field or Save profile button; the profile default belongs in server.toml. Note clipped or unreachable controls as failures even if state assertions pass.

Write a separate visual-review.json with the actual result path, executable hashes, inspected image names and observed scope. Keep failed traces intact.

effects

Configured cursor trails, particles and typing camera affect real terminal pixels and decay without corrupting caret placement.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

For Godot Windows use tests/platform/windows/windows_feature_acceptance.py --suite effects --project <frozen-project> --evidence <fresh-directory>. Its four independently invocable windows_effects_e2e.py modes are controls (default), --pixels, --camera, and --isolation; rerun only the affected mode when repairing a gap. The actual View > Effects dialog edits a validated draft. Rendered tests run on a private Windows desktop and drive a real raw ConPTY fixture. Inspect both dialog scroll positions, paired trail/particle captures, typing camera captures, and the unrelated native window. Require exact PTY input, bounded particles, identical terminal-content pixels after decay, and an independent ray/plane caret projection error below 0.75 pixels. Do not use desktop input or the OS clipboard.

Inspect cursor trails from terminal output

Compare each trail-{smear,blaze,lightning}-peak.png with its matching -after.png. The real terminal application moves its cursor through CUP sequences while the typing camera is disabled. Require visibly different trail styles at the projected terminal cell, a stable terminal sheet/camera, and a clean final image after decay. A changing telemetry flag alone is insufficient. Hiding the application cursor must remove the trail, and no trail may jump between unrelated panes or windows.

Inspect particle presets and configured typing camera

Compare each particles-{dots,fireworks,flames,glitter,sparks}.png against its corresponding -off.png. The preset must contribute visible pixels at the actual caret and removing it must remove only those pixels. Check that the particle count remains bounded and switching preset does not restart the PTY.

Compare typing-configured-peak.png and typing-configured-after.png. With 50% intensity and a configured 2× maximum, the live camera reaches 1.5×. Godot's follow, lean and drift may move the caret on screen: require the independent camera-ray/terminal-plane inverse to recover its unchanged canvas position within 0.75 pixels, as recorded in typing-projection.json. The terminal title and content move together, and configured hold/decay restore the original view. Verify saved controls and rejected out-of-range inputs through the same frontend action path.

Inspect Effects controls

Inspect the Effects dialog captures, opened through the actual View menu. Presets, trail style, intensity, parameter editor and Apply/Cancel must be readable and fit without overlap. The existing Input, Selection and Notifications controls must remain in their prior positions. Record exact images and observations in visual-review.json, keeping failed runs and their executable hashes.

font-rendering

Selectable fonts and ligatures change real glyphs without shifting terminal cells, selection or the shell process.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

For Godot Windows, use python tests/platform/windows/windows_feature_acceptance.py --suite fonts --project <frozen-project> --evidence <new-directory> with GRAFFITTY_TEST_SERVER set to the frozen owner. It drives the actual Fonts dialog and a private PowerShell ConPTY, records exact shaped/Unicode clipboard text, checks real console dimensions and executes a command in the original shell after rejecting and correcting a font. Review paired glyph captures separately from state assertions.

Fonts and terminal cells

Use a fresh offscreen frontend. Disable typing effects so paired captures differ only in the selected font settings. Retain the executable hash, JSONL trace, screenshots and actual copied text.

Observe fonts and ligatures

  1. Print a != b -> c === d in the real terminal, followed by a separate line containing Greek, Korean and a combining accent. Record the pane PID and grid.
  2. Select the bundled JetBrains Mono file with ligatures disabled; capture. Enable ligatures and capture at the same camera position and terminal state.
  3. Inspect the operators: glyph substitutions must be visibly different, while following characters remain on their original cells. Unchanged settings metadata alone cannot establish that shaping works.
  4. Select an installed monospace family, such as Menlo on macOS. Inspect the changed glyph style, fallback Unicode and unchanged terminal layout.

Select and recover

  1. Drag a selection across the shaped operator line. Copy must return the exact original characters, not substituted Unicode symbols or shortened content.
  2. Change the pane font size; compare the live PTY's stty size to the rendered cell grid. Header position, cursor and selection must remain aligned.
  3. Choose a missing font file. Require an explicit error while retaining the current working font and the same live shell. Correct the setting and type another command successfully.
  4. Record actual rendered observations separately from automated test results. Do not claim full bidirectional-script shaping or physical Retina quality from these limited, offscreen checks.

input-routing

Configured keys and terminal wheel events deliver their intended actions and exact PTY bytes without leaking consumed shortcuts or changing speed with font size.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

For Godot on Windows, run python tests/platform/windows/windows_input_acceptance.py --suite input --evidence <new-directory>. It uses private real PowerShell/ConPTY shells and Godot viewport events. Keyboard shortcuts come only from client.toml [bindings]; an empty array unbinds an action so its key reaches the PTY, SendText = [{ key = "F6", text = "…" }] sends exactly that text and Ignore = ["F7"] sends nothing. The app's Edit → Input Settings dialog provides Apply, Cancel, mouse bindings and scroll speed. The fixture covers rejected typed settings without restarting shells. Inspect settings/input-settings.png, wheel/half-row-font-{16,24,32}.png and mouse-controls/mouse-binding-search.png; the last capture shows the literal query and real highlighted matches. --project <isolated-project> selects an isolated extension build. For targeted follow-ups, use the individual cases in tests/platform/windows/windows_input_routing_e2e.py and retain existing unaffected evidence. Do not send desktop input or use the system clipboard.

Verify actual accumulated PTY bytes, including key releases. A custom Unicode text binding must send only its configured text; ignored keys send nothing; a removed default binding reaches the terminal normally. Leader sequences and multi-key sequences consume constituent keys, one-shot tables pop, expired tables pass the ordinary key, and the configured workspace prefix consumes its prefix keys. Open real terminal search through a configured key, type the query through the frontend's keyboard route, and cancel using a remapped modal key. These local keys must not enter the raw PTY.

At font sizes 16, 24 and 32, two 7.5 px wheel motions must produce one row of history scrolling, with the first preserving a half-row. A discrete wheel notch scrolls three rows. Check a multiplier of 2 and a disabled multiplier of 0. In the actual alternate screen, no arrow bytes may be sent when ALT_SCROLL is disabled; with ALT_SCROLL enabled, two fractional events send exactly one arrow. In SGR tracking mode, require the exact wheel packet at the projected cell, and three packets for a discrete notch.

Inspect the search, wheel and Input Settings captures. Search must show the literal query with real matches. Fractional content must remain legible without squeezing or dropped rows. The actual Input dialog must be contained and readable, with the configured bindings and speed visible. Invalid typed settings must preserve the working config and original PTY process. Report unexpected bytes or clipped UI as failures; do not substitute state-only telemetry for image inspection.

Save a separate visual-review.json naming each image actually inspected and the frozen binary digest. These injected events do not establish physical trackpad event delivery or OS-level shortcut behavior.

native-gestures

Zoom-only pinches preserve the cursor anchor; simultaneous panning moves the remembered zoom point without a jump.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Pinch and pan intent

For Godot on Windows, run the production-controller replay on a private desktop:

python tests/platform/windows/windows_private_replay.py \
  --replay tests/llm-e2e/suites/godot/integration/replays/native-gestures.gd \
  --evidence <new-directory>

Use a fresh evidence directory and frozen executables. Never inject OS mouse or keyboard events, take focus, or attach to a personal session.

For zoom-only intent, inspect native-zoom-only.png and the recorded projection requests. The original off-center canvas point must remain under the starting cursor within two projected pixels, even when the cursor position changes during the pinch. Magnification must be applied exactly once (1.2 × 1.1 = 1.32).

For simultaneous zoom and pan, inspect native-zoom-and-pan.png and its trace. A wheel translation of (12, −5) must move the remembered zoom point by (36, −15), using the configured 3× pan speed. The following pinch must stay attached to that moved point within two projected pixels. Compare the actual world and pane edges between captures; no unexpected reset or loss of the terminal is acceptable.

After pinch end, a normal wheel event must leave the gesture controller and return to ordinary terminal scrolling. Record separate PASS/FAIL observations with the executable hash in visual-review.json; a numeric zoom value alone is insufficient. This replay injects gesture events into the production controller. It does not prove that the OS delivers physical trackpad events to an inactive window; that remains a separate device check.

notifications

Terminal notifications retain application actions and owning-pane focus, and configured bells visibly fade without disturbing the human desktop.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

For Godot on Windows, run python tests/platform/windows/windows_private_replay.py --replay tests/llm-e2e/suites/godot/integration/replays/notifications.gd --evidence <new-directory>. It opens the actual Terminal Bell controls (without an in-app notification viewer), records delivery in private helpers, and captures native bell pixels without producing OS notifications or sound.

Use a frozen build and a fresh evidence directory. Never invoke native notification/audio helpers, use the human clipboard or synthesize desktop input.

Inspect notifications and activate the owning pane

Inspect the actual Terminal Bell controls, opened through the Terminal menu: visual bell duration/color and audible preference must be readable and fit without overlapping text. State-only visibility is insufficient.

Require exact OSC99 capability, alive, activation and close replies through the real raw PTY. The capability reply must precede DA1 when both probes occur in the same application write. Activating a notification after another tab gains focus must select the original live pane without replacing its PID. Replacement, expiry, consumed keys and closed-owner keys must reject stale activation. Headless delivery must not launch OS helpers.

Inspect visual bell lifetime

Compare bell-before.png, bell-peak.png, bell-middle.png and bell-after.png. The actual terminal pixels must tint at the peak, diminish at the middle and return to baseline after the configured duration. The terminal contents, title and camera framing must remain readable and stable. A BEL terminating OSC9 must not trigger the bell callback. Enabling audible preference in headless replay records the request without producing sound.

Record inspected files and findings in visual-review.json. Keep every failed run and executable hash. Native OS permission prompts, system audio and native focus activation remain unverified by this private-desktop test.

session-defaults

New local terminals honor typed launch defaults without changing existing sessions or treating environment values as shell commands.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

New terminal launch defaults

Use the private fixture. Set zsh's ZDOTDIR to a fresh empty directory so login-shell testing does not run the user's personal startup scripts. Do not change HOME or use the user's live terminal sessions.

Configure future sessions

  1. Verify the initial shell uses the GUI launch directory. Change it to a different private directory and retain its PID, cwd and a uniquely named environment variable.
  2. Configure /bin/zsh, login enabled, a private directory containing spaces, and a literal environment value containing Unicode and $(not_a_command).
  3. Open Terminal → Session defaults using the actual Godot controls. Inspect session-defaults-dialog.png: shell, login, directory and environment fields are readable; the fields belong to new local sessions and are not presented as remote host settings.

Prove real launch behavior

  1. Create a tab. A subprocess of its actual PTY must report the source shell's current directory, literal configured environment value and parent PID; zsh must report login enabled. The configured initial directory must not override an existing source pane's live cwd.
  2. Change to non-login mode and another literal value, then create a split. The new shell must use those settings without command expansion and inherit its source directory. Change that shell's cwd and create another split; inheritance must still work while the configured initial directory stays set.
  3. Return to the initial shell. Its cwd, environment and process remain the same. Metadata-only defaults do not establish this behavior.
  4. Delete a source directory and create both a split and a tab from that pane. Both actual PTYs must start in the remembered original GUI launch directory. Delete that launch directory too and repeat; both must fall back to the owner's home directory. Descendants must preserve the original fallback.

Reject invalid defaults without mutation

  1. Try a missing executable, missing directory and a protected capability environment override. Each produces a concrete error.
  2. Working defaults and all existing PTY identities/counts stay unchanged.
  3. Preserve failing traces and report unsupported paths explicitly; no clipboard, desktop input or personal startup configuration is needed for this fixture.
Markdown source
# New terminal launch defaults

Use the private fixture. Set zsh's `ZDOTDIR` to a fresh empty directory
so login-shell testing does not run the user's personal startup scripts. Do not
change HOME or use the user's live terminal sessions.

## Configure future sessions

1. Verify the initial shell uses the GUI launch directory. Change it to a
   different private directory and retain its PID, cwd and a uniquely named
   environment variable.
2. Configure `/bin/zsh`, login enabled, a private directory containing spaces,
   and a literal environment value containing Unicode and `$(not_a_command)`.
3. Open Terminal → Session defaults using the actual Godot controls. Inspect
   `session-defaults-dialog.png`: shell, login, directory and environment fields
   are readable; the fields belong to new local sessions and are not presented
   as remote host settings.

## Prove real launch behavior

1. Create a tab. A subprocess of its actual PTY must report the source shell's
   current directory, literal configured environment value and parent PID;
   zsh must report login enabled. The configured initial directory must not
   override an existing source pane's live cwd.
2. Change to non-login mode and another literal value, then create a split.
   The new shell must use those settings without command expansion and inherit
   its source directory. Change that shell's cwd and create another split;
   inheritance must still work while the configured initial directory stays set.
3. Return to the initial shell. Its cwd, environment and process remain the same.
   Metadata-only defaults do not establish this behavior.
4. Delete a source directory and create both a split and a tab from that pane.
   Both actual PTYs must start in the remembered original GUI launch directory.
   Delete that launch directory too and repeat; both must fall back to the
   owner's home directory. Descendants must preserve the original fallback.

## Reject invalid defaults without mutation

1. Try a missing executable, missing directory and a protected capability
   environment override. Each produces a concrete error.
2. Working defaults and all existing PTY identities/counts stay unchanged.
3. Preserve failing traces and report unsupported paths explicitly; no clipboard,
   desktop input or personal startup configuration is needed for this fixture.

status-strips

Overview status strips follow real projected panes, show their own CPU/RAM and agent state, and preserve access to terminal contents and advertised ports.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Overview status strips

For Godot on Windows, run python tests/platform/windows/windows_feature_acceptance.py --suite status-strips --evidence <new-directory>. Use disposable server processes and capture the whole window, since a raw world texture omits screen overlays. Keep normal human desktop input untouched.

Read real per-pane status

  1. Create two panes with different live shell PIDs. Wait for the shared server's actual resource samples; do not inject expected metrics into the UI.
  2. Register an adapter in one pane with an advertised input/output and set its agent state. Keep the other pane a plain shell.
  3. Zoom out until each projected 30px header is shorter than 24 logical pixels, then wait for the camera flight and arrival fade to settle.
  4. Capture the UI. Read each pane's title, CPU and RAM from its visible strip. CPU and RAM must appear side by side on one row, with the pane title above and the optional agent badge below, on desktop and Android. Compare the values with that pane's resource sample, allowing display rounding and normal new samples. Only the adapter pane has an agent badge. Distinct metadata alone does not prove that the text is visibly rendered.

Pan and avoid ports

  1. Pan the overview and slightly change zoom. The strips move with their own projected panes while retaining readable text size.
  2. Inspect all strip rectangles against projected terminal/chromium content, other strips and advertised ports. Content overlap is always a failure. Port overlap is permitted only if every otherwise valid perimeter position requires it; it must not be the first choice when a clear position exists.
  3. Select text or drag a connection near a strip. The strip itself must not capture pointer input or change the focused shell.
  4. Capture at least two camera positions and retain projected geometry and server resource samples beside those images.

Check hidden and unavailable states

  1. Fit a pane: the overview strip disappears when the projected header reaches normal size. Move a pane fully offscreen: it has no floating orphan strip.
  2. Switch tabs and return. Only panes in the active destination show strips; outgoing/arriving surfaces do not leave a stale overlay during the flight.
  3. If a sample is missing, warming up, stale or offline, require an explicit unavailable label/em dash. Unknown usage must never be shown as measured zero. Use a real disconnected test host for the offline state when available.
  4. Report unavailable runtime checks as BLOCKED rather than passed.
Markdown source
# Overview status strips

For Godot on Windows, run `python tests/platform/windows/windows_feature_acceptance.py --suite
status-strips --evidence <new-directory>`. Use disposable server processes and
capture the whole window, since a raw world texture omits screen overlays.
Keep normal human desktop input untouched.

## Read real per-pane status

1. Create two panes with different live shell PIDs. Wait for the shared server's
   actual resource samples; do not inject expected metrics into the UI.
2. Register an adapter in one pane with an advertised input/output and set its
   agent state. Keep the other pane a plain shell.
3. Zoom out until each projected 30px header is shorter than 24 logical pixels,
   then wait for the camera flight and arrival fade to settle.
4. Capture the UI. Read each pane's title, CPU and RAM from its visible strip.
   CPU and RAM must appear side by side on one row, with the pane title above
   and the optional agent badge below, on desktop and Android.
   Compare the values with that pane's resource sample, allowing display
   rounding and normal new samples. Only the adapter pane has an agent badge.
   Distinct metadata alone does not prove that the text is visibly rendered.

## Pan and avoid ports

1. Pan the overview and slightly change zoom. The strips move with their own
   projected panes while retaining readable text size.
2. Inspect all strip rectangles against projected terminal/chromium content,
   other strips and advertised ports. Content overlap is always a failure.
   Port overlap is permitted only if every otherwise valid perimeter position
   requires it; it must not be the first choice when a clear position exists.
3. Select text or drag a connection near a strip. The strip itself must not
   capture pointer input or change the focused shell.
4. Capture at least two camera positions and retain projected geometry and
   server resource samples beside those images.

## Check hidden and unavailable states

1. Fit a pane: the overview strip disappears when the projected header reaches
   normal size. Move a pane fully offscreen: it has no floating orphan strip.
2. Switch tabs and return. Only panes in the active destination show strips;
   outgoing/arriving surfaces do not leave a stale overlay during the flight.
3. If a sample is missing, warming up, stale or offline, require an explicit
   unavailable label/em dash. Unknown usage must never be shown as measured
   zero. Use a real disconnected test host for the offline state when available.
4. Report unavailable runtime checks as BLOCKED rather than passed.

LLM suite specification

For Godot Windows, run python tests/platform/windows/windows_feature_acceptance.py --suite workspace-controls --project <frozen-project> --evidence <new-directory> with GRAFFITTY_TEST_SERVER and GRAFFITTY_CHROMIUM_HOST set to the frozen owner and CEF helper. The fixture sends native file-drop events to a real raw PTY and compares every received byte, including quoting, Unicode and separator bytes. Godot file drops must not append a trailing separator. The command-like filename is literal data; it must not execute or add a submitting newline. Modal and chromium focus must suppress terminal drops.

Inspect monitor-dragged.png: the monitor is an independent readable panel at the dragged position. It must show the correct live terminal process identity and peak memory, and keep following owner samples. Godot's monitor is a mod (docs/developers/automation-and-extensions/mods.md): it omits the interval and Select all / Copy selection / Resume updates buttons, and its text cannot be selected or copied. The monitor must block terminal wheel/native gestures only in its actual rectangle.

Inspect messages-selectable-error.png and messages-open-log.png: the rejected Unicode font path is readable in bounded retained history, selectable/copyable, and present in the actual private frontend log. The Open log button stays within the application. No unreadable labels, clipped controls, missing Unicode, or terminal input leaking from the dialog is acceptable.

Inspect monitor-chromium-resources.png: the focused Chromium has its own measured resource identity and a real running sample rather than the owner's shell values. Require the actual decoded chromium and RPC assertions as well as the image.

Record a separate visual-review.json with the executable hash, exact files inspected, PASS/FAIL per condition and any limitations. Headless native event replay does not establish physical Finder drag-and-drop or native macOS clipboard integration. Do not mark unavailable resource data as measured zero, or convert fixture/renderer failures into PASS.

LLM suite specification

Live terminals inside a 3D world

Use disposable configuration and fresh shell processes. The fixture shell is /bin/sh; never type test commands into the user's existing session. Evidence must include terminal history or screen state from the real terminal backend, not an expected string inserted into the UI model.

Use a real shell

  1. Type a command that prints a random test marker, $$, and pwd.
  2. Wait for output and verify the marker from a completed output line, the PID against backend process metadata, and the isolated working directory.
  3. Print Unicode, ANSI colors, and an OSC title. Confirm the title and visible glyphs update in the application. Capture the rendered terminal and UI.
  4. Change the cursor shape with DECSCUSR. The backend and drawn cursor agree.

Split and resize

  1. Split horizontally, then vertically. Each new terminal has a distinct live process, and focus routes input to exactly one pane.
  2. Resize the split. Compare the real terminal rows/columns (stty size) with the intended pane area. Merely clipping a pane offscreen must not resize it.
  3. Drag one pane outside the main area, fit it by double-clicking its title, restore its prior view, and bring it back. Its PID and output survive.
  4. Close that pane. Its process ends; all other panes continue responding.

Inspect weighted layouts and tab transfer

  1. Enable horizontal tiling with two live terminals. Drag the divider and inspect the changed widths; drag to the edge and confirm neither pane collapses. Undo and redo restore the exact divider position and the original processes.
  2. Split one pane vertically. Drag its title onto another pane's bottom edge. Inspect tiling-drop-preview.png: two distinct preview colors identify the proposed regions. Compare tiling-drop-committed.png; their boundaries must match the proposal. Undo restores the nested arrangement.
  3. Open a chromium beside a terminal and type into its page. Drag the terminal's title onto another tab using the visible tab bar. Inspect the arriving terminal and chromium: the page's existing state and terminal output remain.
  4. Move the chromium alone into a new tab. Inspect the recognizable page in surface-chromium-only-tab.png; its content remains proportional. Undo/redo must restore the same tab identity, not recreate the Chromium document.
  5. Create and close a terminal in that chromium-only tab. The page stays alive. Then close its original owner from another tab; the chromium and newly empty presentation tab disappear while an unrelated shell remains usable.

Navigate independent tabs

  1. Create another tab, change its zoom and pan, and return to the first tab.
  2. The first tab retains its layout and camera view. Reorder the second tab; its live shell moves with it to the destination assigned to its new index.
  3. Switch tabs during a flight, then type immediately after arrival. Input reaches the visible focused pane, with no duplicate or leaked characters.

Inspect scrolling and input

  1. Produce at least 100 numbered lines. Scroll half a row using the same input route as a trackpad; capture the top and bottom partial rows and scrollbar.
  2. Enter an alternate-screen application or deterministic alternate-screen fixture. It retains its full grid and receives appropriate mouse/scroll input. It does not expose unrelated main-screen scrollback.
  3. Select Unicode text and copy it. Paste text through bracketed-paste mode; verify exact received bytes using a raw-PTY fixture.
  4. Report unsupported actions as BLOCKED. They do not count as passed feature parity, even when the smaller automated smoke scenario passes.

background-gestures

Delivered gestures target their intended window without changing keyboard focus; macOS hardware pinch requires focusing the window first.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Gesture routing and keyboard focus

On macOS, focus the Graffitty window before pinching, then move both fingers without lifting to pan. Native pinch recognition requires an active window; unfocused pinch is not supported. Ordinary two-finger scrolling over an inactive window should continue to work.

The replay uses two native windows and sends the AppKit bridge's gesture payload through Input.parse_input_event, including its target window and physical pixel coordinates, checking navigation, focus ownership and active/idle frame limits. It verifies routing of an already-delivered gesture, not hardware pinch delivery to an inactive application. Injected events must target their intended window without changing keyboard focus. After the gesture, that window should return to its inactive frame limit.

Run python3 tests/platform/macos/test_macos_trackpad.py for the native pinch lifecycle, continuous pan, release, and cancellation. Physical trackpad checks should focus the window first; synthetic input cannot establish native event delivery.

rubber-band

A terminal pulled past either end of its scrollback stretches under the fingers and springs back on release, as Chromium's rubber band does.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Terminal rubber band

Fill scrollback with numbered rows. With two fingers on a trackpad (or one finger on a touchscreen), scroll to the top and keep pulling: the text must follow the fingers at about a twentieth of their travel, leaving an empty band of the terminal background above the first row, while the viewport stays on the first row. Lift the fingers after resting: the text springs back smoothly and settles exactly where it was. Repeat at the live bottom, where the band opens below the prompt.

Flick into an edge so momentum carries the content there: it must overshoot briefly and return, never stay displaced. Pull, then scroll back the other way without lifting: the pull is given up first, and only then does the content scroll.

A mouse wheel must never stretch the content, however fast it turns. Vim and other alternate-screen or mouse-reporting applications must not stretch either. A terminal with nothing to scroll yet still pulls, both up and down. The look is the same on every platform.

The replay injects pan gestures carrying Chromium's scroll phases and checks the pull distance against the one-twentieth mapping, the empty band in the rendered frame, the unchanged viewport row, the release settling at zero, the momentum bounce, giving the pull up before scrolling, and that unphased, wheel and alternate-screen scrolling leave the content in place.

Fractional terminal scrolling

Fill scrollback with numbered, alternating coloured rows. Slowly scroll with two fingers: the first small movement must move text, and stopping must allow a partial row. local-chromium-shared-gpu

MUST render same-host chromium frames through verified shared GPU imports, with no video/JPEG/PNG encode-decode transport.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Local chromium shared GPU — MT-01

This is a strict requirement governed by the suite contract.

Verify native sharing and rendered chromium content

  1. Start an isolated real session server and a separate production frontend on the same host, using a supported GPU-sharing configuration. Record both build identities, PIDs, frontend, OS, GPU and connection mechanism. Keep the user's existing server and workspace untouched.
  2. Open a real chromium through the frontend. Use a local fixture page with four distinct colored regions, text input and a visibly increasing frame counter. Record the actual rendered frontend continuously. Type Unicode, scroll, and click a control; verify the resulting DOM state and visible updates.
  3. Inspect the actual server-to-client transport. Require a native resource exchange and successful client GPU import, and correlate the imported texture and its dimensions/generation with rendered fixture content. A server capture label such as captureTransport=iosurface proves only capture, not client import.
  4. For this chromium/session, require zero encoded JPEG/PNG/video frame payloads to this client and zero transport image/video encodes and decodes attributable to local presentation. Exclude the fixture's own web assets and unrelated remote subscribers from these counters; retain that scoping in the evidence. Renaming an encoded payload or uploading CPU-decoded pixels to the GPU fails.
  5. Repeat with a frontend capable of hardware video decode. Video capability must not cause local presentation to choose HEVC/H.264/AV1 instead of shared GPU resources. Do not certify this from a synthetic Python client alone.

Exercise resize, reconnect and resource lifetime

  1. Resize the chromium repeatedly while it animates. Verify correct content and dimensions, a valid new resource generation, no stale frames and no import errors. Record imports/releases to establish that old handles are retired.
  2. Disconnect the frontend without closing the server-owned chromium. Reattach a fresh frontend process; verify preserved DOM state, a fresh valid resource exchange and continuing animation without an encoded startup-frame fallback.
  3. Close the chromium and frontend. Verify their imported resources are released and unrelated PTYs remain alive. Record the cleanup results.
  4. Review the recording alongside the telemetry. Report PASS only when both visual behavior and verified shared GPU delivery satisfy every step.

JPEG/PNG compatibility delivery and video streaming fail this local case even if they look correct or are fast. Unsupported native import belongs to MT-03 and must not disguise missing support for a claimed supported local configuration. Missing import/counter evidence is BLOCKED, not inferred success.

local-kitty-decode-once

MUST decode Kitty PNG uploads once on the server and deliver verified pixels over shared memory or IPC without client PNG decoding, including reconnect.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Local Kitty images decode once — MT-02

This is a strict requirement governed by the suite contract.

Verify live image delivery without client PNG decoding

  1. Start an isolated real server, PTY and separate production frontend on the same host. Record build identities and the negotiated image transport. Record the actual frontend throughout the case.
  2. Generate a fresh PNG fixture with known RGBA pixels, transparency and distinct colored regions. Use a unique fixture per run to avoid a prewarmed decode cache hiding work. Record its dimensions and source/decoded-pixel hashes.
  3. Emit a real Kitty inline PNG upload from the PTY with an explicit image ID and placement. Observe the image in the terminal and inspect per-image counters: exactly one server PNG decode and zero client PNG decodes for that upload.
  4. Require delivery of server-decoded pixels through shared memory or IPC. Verify the client's imported/mapped/received pixel hash and dimensions against the fixture, as well as the visible placement and transparency. No image, an empty payload, or an alleged shared-memory reference without actual mapping fails. PNG (f=100) replay to the local client fails even if a decoder cache avoids work on a later attempt. Sending decoded raw Kitty pixels over IPC is allowed; sharing a GPU texture is not required for this image case.
  5. Repeat with a new fixture via a server-side temporary-file Kitty upload. Verify the server consumes/deletes the source and that the frontend does not reopen its path. Use a second attached client: both must render the same image without another PNG decode or independently resolving a server path.

Verify reconnect, replacement and cleanup

  1. After the source file is gone, detach the frontend and start a fresh process. Reattach to the same PTY. Require identical pixels and placement, no repeated server decode for the retained image, and zero client PNG decodes.
  2. Replace the same image ID with a fresh fixture. Verify new pixels replace the old pixels on both clients, with one decode for the new upload and no stale shared-memory generation. Delete the image through Kitty and verify it vanishes.
  3. Close clients and the test PTY. Verify handles/mappings and server image storage are released when no longer referenced, without affecting unrelated sessions.
  4. Review the recording and scoped decode/mapping evidence for every step. Report PASS only when real frontend rendering and the decode-once transport both pass.

The repository-root tests/support/local_media_e2e.py --case kitty --evidence NEW_DIRECTORY can diagnose live/reconnect PNG replay. It is supporting evidence, not an LLM run, and currently does not cover actual GUI rendering or SHM lifetime.

   sharing a GPU texture is not required for this image case.
5. Repeat with a new fixture via a server-side temporary-file Kitty upload. Verify
   the server consumes/deletes the source and that the frontend does not reopen
   its path. Use a second attached client: both must render the same image without
   another PNG decode or independently resolving a server path.

## Verify reconnect, replacement and cleanup

1. After the source file is gone, detach the frontend and start a fresh process.
   Reattach to the same PTY. Require identical pixels and placement, no repeated
   server decode for the retained image, and zero client PNG decodes.
2. Replace the same image ID with a fresh fixture. Verify new pixels replace the
   old pixels on both clients, with one decode for the new upload and no stale
   shared-memory generation. Delete the image through Kitty and verify it vanishes.
3. Close clients and the test PTY. Verify handles/mappings and server image storage
   are released when no longer referenced, without affecting unrelated sessions.
4. Review the recording and scoped decode/mapping evidence for every step. Report
   PASS only when real frontend rendering and the decode-once transport both pass.

can diagnose live/reconnect PNG replay. It is supporting evidence, not an LLM run,
and currently does not cover actual GUI rendering or SHM lifetime.

   handle values, a claimed PID, server flags and readable-looking paths are not
   proof. Ordinary SSH byte forwarding cannot transfer ancillary descriptors or
   Mach rights. Verify failed exchange/import is detected with bounded time and

Local remote-control client

# Local remote-control client

local-startup

MUST open one fresh local session in the launch/configured directory without server setup or a Connect form; explicit attachment preserves existing shells and initializes empty workspaces.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

Automatic local startup

This is a strict shared product requirement. A local user opens the application and gets a terminal; the server/client architecture must not require them to set up a server, enter an endpoint/password, or click Connect. Run and report this case independently for every required frontend.

Automatic local launch

  1. Use isolated application config/state and the production development launcher (mise dev for Godot), with no existing test server or connection descriptor. Do not stop the user's normal server or modify their workspace.
  2. Record the complete launch. Require automatic local owner startup, authenticated attachment and a visible focused terminal, without any connection/setup form.
  3. Type a unique marker and verify output. Record server/PTY identities and the frontend build. The terminal must be usable immediately after startup.
  4. Launch again with --new-session from a different directory. Require a fresh server session with exactly one pane in that directory (or the explicitly configured directory). The first session and its shell must remain intact.
  5. Launch again without arguments. The application's first window returns to the session a frontend showed last, with the same panes and no new shell.

Empty workspace recovery and retained sessions

  1. Prepare an empty workspace fixture before its first terminal is created. Explicitly select that workspace. Require automatic creation of one usable terminal; an empty initial workspace must not show the remote Connect form. Closing the last pane of an established live session instead removes that session, as specified in last-session shutdown.
  2. Repeat with an existing live terminal containing a unique marker. Detach and use gft session attach -t NAME to reopen it; require the same terminal ID, shell PID and retained output, with no duplicate terminal created.
  3. On a freshly opened window, the Main View border stays hidden throughout startup. Zoom out to reveal it and return to Main View to hide it again. Type into the terminal: configured camera tilt and depth-of-field effects must still work when the server's page size differs from the window size. Resize the local desktop window between portrait and landscape: its tiled main area must fill both available dimensions, with additional terminal rows or columns instead of a scaled, fixed-size page. The server must retain that updated area. Remote mirrors keep fitting the shared area without resizing the owner's PTY just because their own window or on-screen keyboard changes.
  4. Close the last pane with the pane shortcut, then repeat in a fresh session with the tab shortcut and with shell exit. Each closes that window; the final window quits the application. No replacement shell may be created, and other windows and their shells must remain alive. The closed session must be removed from the live session inventory; closing the server's final live session must also stop the server automatically. Follow the linked lifecycle case to verify server exit before fixture cleanup.
  5. Keep the connection dialog under observation throughout, including transient appearances. No credentials, endpoint entry or Connect click is allowed.
  6. Close only the test frontend and clean up the owned test resources. Report PASS only with the recording and session evidence; unexpected errors fail.

tests/godot/local_startup_e2e.py is a supporting Godot regression: it creates an empty workspace on a real isolated owner, loads the production entry scene, checks no connection dialog appears, sends real terminal input, and verifies explicit reattachment preserves the shell without duplication, then verifies two --new-session launches get independent single-pane sessions and the correct cwd, and an ordinary launch returns to the session shown last. With --gpu, it also checks 85% background opacity using a hidden Metal window. The --scenario close-pane, close-tab, and shell-exit cases check startup framing and natural application exit. With --gpu, they also send real keyboard input and compare rendered text with depth-of-field enabled and disabled at the same camera pose. It does not certify visible keyboard focus or the other frontends.
