title-double-click

Title clicks preserve tiling; double-click shares the keyboard fit/restore toggle, including the 30% no-history fallback, at every zoom level without changing sessions or layout.

✅ pass · 39.2 s · AV1 · 2026-10-04T17:00+09:00

LLM suite specification

Title double-click navigation

Launch mise run dev -- --shell=/bin/sh with an isolated test config. Record continuous motion for animation checks, capture before/after layouts, and report PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with observations. Use actual title-bar clicks, including the first click of each double-click; do not substitute a menu command or API call for the behavior under test.

First launch without view history

Before any navigation in a fresh session, double-click the already fitted pane title. Animate to a centered view fitting it within 30% of usable viewport width and height, preserving aspect ratio and pane geometry. Double-click again to restore the fitted view. Repeat by mixing the title double-click with Command+Enter on macOS or Ctrl+Shift+Enter on Linux/Windows; both must use the same saved view.

Single pane and clicks

Start with one tiled terminal, label it ALPHA, and note echo $$. Zoom out and pan off center. Click its compact title once, hold briefly without moving, then release. It must keep its tiled rectangle and membership throughout the press and release. Tiny pointer jitter must not detach it. Double-click its title: the camera must animate back to Main View, with the whole main area visible. Double-click again to restore the exact off-center pan and zoom. The pane must not move or resize. Repeat on its normal title bar at readable scale. Ordinary focus changes are allowed; a single click must not change tiling or navigation. Confirm a deliberate title drag still works, then restore the layout before continuing.

Two panes at every zoom

Split ALPHA horizontally into left and right panes. Label the new pane BETA and note its PID. From a small overview, normal scale, and an enlarged view with the title still visible, single-click then double-click each title. Both panes span the main area's height, so the first double-click from a distinct view must animate to Main View. The next double-click must restore that exact previous view. The first click must not remove the pane from tiling or shift the title away before the second click. Check for a visible intermediate camera position and a smooth arrival, with no snap or leftover drag.

Repeat in another tab with a vertical split: top and bottom panes span the main area's width, so both must return to Main View. Normal tiling gaps count as part of the main-area framing; they must not cause an individual-pane zoom.

Three panes and interruption

Return to the left/right layout and split BETA vertically, making one full-height pane on the left and two half-height panes on the right. Double-click the left title: show Main View. Double-click either right title: animate to fit that individual pane below the toolbar, with its full title and controls visible. Repeat with compact and normal titles.

Return to Main View and focus a smaller right pane's terminal. Press Command+Enter on macOS or Ctrl+Shift+Enter on Linux/Windows without a prefix: View → Fit to Pane must animate to the same framing as its title double-click, retaining keyboard focus and leaving pane geometry unchanged. Double-click to return to the frame saved by the shortcut, then double-click to fit and use the shortcut to restore. Repeated double-clicks must toggle instead of continually fitting.

During a fit animation, pinch or use Command/Ctrl-scroll to zoom manually. The camera must follow the new input immediately and must not jump to the old animation target later. Repeat by choosing View → Fit to Main Area during an animation. Confirm pane rectangles, tiling membership, tab membership, and all original shell PIDs are preserved by navigation. A stashed pane outside the main area must still fit individually even if its width or height matches the main area's dimensions.

Automated replay: replays/title-double-click.gd. Headless checks verify click routing, intermediate camera state, final framing, layout preservation, and interruption; assess visual smoothness from the continuous recording.

window-close-policy

Window close always asks with Cancel focused; Detach keeps sessions, Kill Server ends the local server, and remote windows only detach.

not recorded · — s · UNVERIFIED ·

LLM suite specification

For Godot, run python3 tests/godot/tab_window_e2e.py --scenario close and --scenario close-server, each with a fresh, short --evidence directory. Use the private server, real shells, private Chromium surface and loopback remote host. Do not send desktop input to personal windows or rebuild any executable during the test.

In Godot, × never ends a session, not even one idle pane: it always asks. Local windows offer exactly Kill Server (서버 강제 종료), Detach and Cancel, with Cancel focused; Enter cancels, as does Escape. Both preserve exact shell/job birth identities. Inspect the actual dialog capture for readable warning text and separate buttons. Detach closes only the window and keeps every session and shell alive; detaching the final window quits the app while the server keeps running. Kill Server ends attached and detached sessions on that local server, which then exits. Remote windows offer only Detach and Cancel and must not offer server shutdown; the server must reject close_server from WebSocket clients, even authenticated loopback clients. test_live_sessions.py exercises that rejection, local cleanup, and survival of a separate remote server using disposable real servers.

Compare forced hollow, hidden, application block and unfocused cursor images. Forced hollow must have visible edges and an empty center even while the application requests a bar. Under auto, the application block must appear normally; losing window focus makes that same cursor hollow. Keep these claims distinct from unverified native hardware focus events. zoomed-text-stays-sharp

Zooming the camera in, by typing or by pinching, keeps terminal text as crisp as at rest: glyph edges stay sharp instead of turning into a blurred or pixelated enlargement.

✅ pass · 58.7 s · AV1 · 2026-11-17T22:25+09:00

LLM suite specification

Zoomed text stays sharp

Zooming used to enlarge a texture rendered for the resting view, so text got softer the closer the camera came.

Print text and look at rest

  1. Launch from the repository root:

    mise run dev -- --shell=/bin/sh

    Configure the fixed typing zoom first (adaptive framing is the default): [effects.camera] with zoom_mode = "typing" and zoom = 1.15.

  2. Run echo The quick brown fox jumps over 0123456789 and wait until the camera has settled back to rest.

  3. Take a screenshot of the printed line. This is the reference: note how many screen pixels a glyph edge takes to go from background to text.

Zoom in by pinching

  1. Over the printed line, pinch outward until the text is about three times larger, and wait a second.
  2. Take a screenshot of the same line.
  3. Expected: the glyph edges are as crisp as in the reference. Enlarged but blurry edges, or visible square pixels, fail.
  4. Pinch further, to about five times, and repeat. Expected: still crisp.
  5. Type a few characters so the typing zoom engages, and check the text around the cursor the same way.

Compare with Bistro

  1. Choose View > World > Bistro (BLOCKED if missing).
  2. Repeat the pinch and typing checks on a Bistro wall. Depth of field may soften text away from the cursor; the text at the cursor must be crisp.
  3. Report PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED with the reference and zoomed screenshots side by side at the same on-screen size.
Markdown source
# Zoomed text stays sharp

Zooming used to enlarge a texture rendered for the resting view, so text got
softer the closer the camera came.

## Print text and look at rest

1. Launch from the repository root:

   ```sh
   mise run dev -- --shell=/bin/sh
   ```

   Configure the fixed typing zoom first (adaptive framing is the default):
   `[effects.camera]` with `zoom_mode = "typing"` and `zoom = 1.15`.

2. Run `echo The quick brown fox jumps over 0123456789` and wait until the
   camera has settled back to rest.
3. Take a screenshot of the printed line. This is the reference: note how many
   screen pixels a glyph edge takes to go from background to text.

## Zoom in by pinching

1. Over the printed line, pinch outward until the text is about three times
   larger, and wait a second.
2. Take a screenshot of the same line.
3. Expected: the glyph edges are as crisp as in the reference. Enlarged but
   blurry edges, or visible square pixels, fail.
4. Pinch further, to about five times, and repeat. Expected: still crisp.
5. Type a few characters so the typing zoom engages, and check the text around
   the cursor the same way.

## Compare with Bistro

1. Choose **View > World > Bistro** (BLOCKED if missing).
2. Repeat the pinch and typing checks on a Bistro wall. Depth of field may soften
   text away from the cursor; the text at the cursor must be crisp.
3. Report PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED with the reference and zoomed screenshots side
   by side at the same on-screen size.

Use an isolated owner and Windows D3D12 frontend at the desktop display scaling.

Markdown source
# Korean IME and native windows at 150% scaling

Windows-only supplement to the shared suites. Use isolated D: state and evidence; do not alter personal profiles. Report each shell separately.

## Verify the physical desktop setup

Record Windows display scaling (150%), display resolution, Korean IME selection, Godot renderer and dev build identity. Use an actual visible desktop window. Do not change layout scaling or redesign typing zoom to satisfy this case.

## Compose Korean through the IME

In separate PowerShell 5.1 and 7 panes, use physical Korean IME composition to enter 한글 입력 테스트. Observe composition underline and candidate placement, commit once, backspace a composed syllable, switch to Latin input, and verify exact text without duplicates. Repeat in Neovim. Injecting finished Unicode strings does not pass this stage.

Record the exact Godot version. Godot 4.7.2 has an upstream Windows IME
regression that can turn this phrase into `글 력 트`: committed syllables disappear
even in a standalone `LineEdit`. See [Godot #123269](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/123269)
and [the upstream fix](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123274).
This is a failure on that runtime, not a platform exception. Retain the failed
recording and rerun composition after changing the runtime. Native virtual-key
automation can reproduce it through the OS IME; it does not certify the separate
physical-keyboard and candidate-placement review.

## Exercise native focus and window chrome

Resize, maximize, restore and move the native Graffitty window. Drag a tab into a new native window and back, checking PID continuity. Open a live Chromium pane externally, move that window, return to the pane and verify the same chromium session. Check focus, Ctrl+C, clipboard and window controls on the interactive desktop.

## Review scaling and camera behavior

Review mid-drag and final frames for correct hit targets, legible glyphs and correctly placed IME candidates. Where the demo requires it, disable camera zoom, pane zoom and tilt; retain the known physical-pixel layout model. Record evidence paths and distinguish synthetic replay checks from physical-input review.

Start an isolated Windows PowerShell 5.1 pane

Exercise Unicode cwd and filetree

Exercise input and interrupts

# Windows PowerShell 5.1

Windows-only supplement to the shared suites. Use isolated D: state and evidence; do not alter personal profiles. Report each shell separately.

## Start an isolated Windows PowerShell 5.1 pane

Use a private server config with `[terminal] shell = ["powershell.exe", "-NoLogo"]` and `shell_integration = true`. Start the current dev Godot client in the interactive desktop. Print `$PSVersionTable.PSVersion` and assert major 5, minor 1. Record the actual executable path, server PID and loaded ConPTY DLL path. The prompt must stay alive. Repeat with shell integration disabled: the interactive shell must still remain usable.

## Exercise Unicode cwd and filetree

Create a private directory on D: named `한글 space % #`. Use `Set-Location -LiteralPath` to enter it. Print `(Get-Location).Path` and `한글 Ω 😀`; inspect rendered text and the server-reported cwd. Open the filetree through its header button, verify its root, change directory and verify following. Rename a text file in the Fyler buffer and open it in real Neovim. No warning dialog is allowed.

## Exercise input and interrupts

Type and edit a multiline PowerShell command, run it once and verify exact output. Run a long foreground loop, press physical Ctrl+C, and confirm it stops while the same shell PID survives. Verify Ctrl+Shift+C copy with selection separately from Ctrl+C interrupt without selection. Run the Windows hook test for this shell and retain its verbose output.

## Review the native recording

Record startup, typing, cwd following and interruption continuously. Inspect clear frames at 150% Windows scaling. Record PASS only with assertions plus visual review; synthetic Unicode text input does not certify Korean IME composition.
